# cloud_migrate_layout - move a device off the original cloud folder layout.
#
# The first layout put everything under /GAMES, with the settings backups nested
# inside the saves folder at /GAMES/backup. Both are wrong in ways that bite:
#
#   - /GAMES is a name somebody may well have used for something else, and we
#     write into it as though it were ours.
#   - a backup folder inside the saves folder is inside the path that a `sync`
#     backup mirrors, so the archive is deletable by the operation meant to
#     protect it.
#
# The default has been /ROCKNIX/Saves and /ROCKNIX/Backups since b35c5832b1,
# but cloud_sync_helper only ever adds keys that are missing -- it never
# rewrites one already in the file -- so every device configured before that
# is still on the old layout and will stay there for ever unless asked.
#
# This is an offer, never automatic. Where somebody's saves live is theirs to
# decide, and the safe answer is always to leave it alone.
#
#   cloud_migrate_layout --check     what would move, and whether it is safe
#   cloud_migrate_layout --apply     do it
#   cloud_migrate_layout --state     one line per fact, for the interface to decide
#                                    what to offer (STATE=current|kept|superseded-with-files|
#                                    superseded-empty|own|no-remote; fork #353)
#   cloud_migrate_layout --keep      record that this device keeps its superseded
#                                    folder (LAYOUT_KEEP in the conf; asked once, D-CLOUD-160)
#   cloud_migrate_layout --superseded  the superseded defaults, one per line (no network)
#   cloud_migrate_layout --needs-step  0 when the cloud folder step has something to settle:
#                                    an earlier default, not kept, a remote set up (no
#                                    network; asked at every boot, D-CLOUD-170)
#   cloud_migrate_layout --follow    re-point a device on a superseded default at the
#                                    current layout when another device has already
#                                    made it (no question; D-CLOUD-160's "the other
#                                    devices follow"); 0 when it did, 3 when there was
#                                    nothing to follow
#   cloud_migrate_layout --join      point a device whose own folder holds no saves --
#                                    the current default, or a default this project once
#                                    shipped -- at the earlier folder that does hold them
#                                    (no question; a fresh install, or a carried /GAMES,
#                                    beside a fleet still on the earlier folder); 0 when
#                                    it did, 3 when there was nothing to join
#   cloud_migrate_layout --settle    the seeding's step (cloud_setup --seed-folders):
#                                    --join, else a carried default with nothing in it
#                                    anywhere is pointed at the current folders, which
#                                    the seeding then makes, as for any new cloud
#
# Only the two folders we wrote are moved. Anything else under the old folder
# is left exactly where it is, because it is not ours.

. /etc/profile 2>/dev/null

SYNC_CONF="/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf"
NEW_SAVES="/pixelelated/Saves"
NEW_BACKUPS="/pixelelated/Backups"
NEW_CONTENT="/pixelelated/Content"
NEW_ROOT="${NEW_SAVES%/*}"   # the folder the tiers move into; named by the plan line below
# Every saves folder this project ever shipped as its default. A device whose
# saves folder is one of these is on a layout it never chose, so the move is
# offered (D-CLOUD-160); any other folder is the player's own and stays
# (the sibling-layout branch below). Oldest first; the current default is
# NEW_SAVES and is not listed.
SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES=("/GAMES" "/ROCKNIX/Saves")
# The marker a cloud carries once it is on the current layout (#356): one
# line, layout=<n>, at the parent of the saves folder. Read before anything
# is offered; written after a move or a seeding.
LAYOUT_VERSION=2
LAYOUT_MARKER=".layout"
REMOTE_LAYOUT=0
MIGRATION_RECORD="/storage/.config/cloud-layout-migration.json"
MIGRATION_ACTIVE=0
MIGRATION_RESUMING=0

# Which superseded default's saves folder holds files in this cloud, the
# configured one first, then the others newest first: into SOURCE_FOUND,
# empty when none does. Called directly, never inside $(...): its listings
# stop the run when the cloud cannot be read (list_or_stop), and inside a
# substitution that stop ended only the subshell -- a listing that failed
# read as "no folder holds the saves", a provider error taken for absence,
# and --state then said superseded-empty and the interface offered CREATE
# IT (found 2026-10-01 reading for the mixed-installation test).
SOURCE_FOUND=""
superseded_source() { # <remote> <configured saves folder>
    local remote="$1" saves="$2"
    SOURCE_FOUND=""
    if has_files "${remote}${saves}/"; then SOURCE_FOUND="${saves}"; return 0; fi
    earlier_source "${remote}" "${saves}"
}

# The newest superseded default, other than <except>, whose saves folder
# holds files: into SOURCE_FOUND. Newest first, because where both an
# upstream /GAMES and the fork's /ROCKNIX/Saves hold saves, the fork's is
# the one its other devices write.
earlier_source() { # <remote> [except]
    local remote="$1" except="${2:-}" i s
    SOURCE_FOUND=""
    for (( i = ${#SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]} - 1; i >= 0; i-- )); do
        s="${SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[i]}"
        [ -n "${except}" ] && same_folder "${s}" "${except}" && continue
        if has_files "${remote}${s}/"; then SOURCE_FOUND="${s}"; return 0; fi
    done
    return 1
}

# The pointers of the layout an earlier saves folder belongs to, into
# E_SAVES E_BACKUPS E_CONTENT: its siblings, or the nested /GAMES/backup of
# the first layout. Content goes with it only where this device's own was
# unset or the current default; a folder the player chose for ROMs stays
# theirs.
# An explicit empty CONTENT_REMOTE is the cloud root, not an unset option.
content_unset() { ! grep -q '^CONTENT_REMOTE=' "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null; }

# A pointer-only transition may follow an empty default backup tier, never
# abandon its archives or replace a custom folder. Called directly: failed
# listings terminate the caller through list_or_stop, not a subshell.
backup_pointer_for() { # <remote> <configured backups> <destination default>
    local remote="$1" backups="$2" target="$3" known=0
    NEXT_BACKUPS="${backups}"
    case "${backups%/}" in
        ""|/GAMES/backup|/ROCKNIX/Backups|/pixelelated/Backups) known=1 ;;
    esac
    [ "${known}" -eq 1 ] || return 0
    if [ -n "${backups}" ]; then
        list_or_stop "${remote}${backups%/}/" --files-only -R --include '*.{zip,tar.gz}'
        [ -n "${LISTING}" ] && return 0
    fi
    NEXT_BACKUPS="${target}"
}

earlier_layout() { # <saves folder> <this device's content pointer>
    local src="$1" content="$2" parent
    parent="${src%/*}"; [ -n "${parent}" ] || parent="${src}"
    E_SAVES="${src}"
    if [ "${src}" = "/GAMES" ]; then E_BACKUPS="/GAMES/backup"; else E_BACKUPS="${parent}/Backups"; fi
    if content_unset || same_folder "${content}" "${NEW_CONTENT}"; then
        E_CONTENT="${parent}/Content"
    else
        E_CONTENT="${content}"
    fi
}

superseded_default() { # <saves folder>: 0 when it is a default this project once shipped
    local s
    for s in "${SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]}"; do same_folder "$1" "${s}" && return 0; done
    return 1
}

say() { echo "$@"; }

remote_name() {
    rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1
}

# The shared reader (cloud_setup's, the content scripts', D-CLOUD-149): a
# single-quoted or bare pointer used to come back as the whole line from
# `cut -d'"' -f2`, and the new folder logic then moved the pointer off the
# player's saves (the audit of the fixes, claude G3-D-05).
conf_get() { # <KEY> (the content scripts' reader, mirrored so every reader agrees, D-CLOUD-149): its value, quotes off; nothing when absent; exit 2 when unreadable, and why on stdout
    [ -f ${SYNC_CONF} ] || return 0
    awk -v k="$1" '
        { t = $0; gsub(/\t/, "", t); if (t ~ /[[:cntrl:]]/ && !cntrl) cntrl = NR }
        index($0, k "=") != 1 && !other \
            && $0 ~ ("^[ \t]*((export|declare|typeset|readonly|local)([ \t]+-[A-Za-z]+)*[ \t]+)?" k "[ \t]*[+]?=") { other = NR }
        index($0, k "=") == 1 {
            s = substr($0, length(k) + 2); v = ""; r = ""; ok = 1; why = ""
            c = substr(s, 1, 1)
            if (c == "\"") {
                # Inside double quotes bash reads \" \\ \$ and \` as the one
                # character each (PL-015), and so does this; an unescaped $
                # or backtick is an expansion this reader does not make, and
                # any other backslash is refused as conf_valid refuses it.
                n = length(s); i = 2; closed = 0
                while (i <= n) {
                    d = substr(s, i, 1)
                    if (d == "\"") { closed = 1; break }
                    if (d == "\\") {
                        e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
                        if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
                        ok = 0
                        why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
                                        : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
                        break
                    }
                    if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
                    v = v d; i++
                }
                if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
                if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
            } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
                j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
                if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
            } else {
                match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
            }
            if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
            if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }
        }
        END {
            if (cntrl) { print "line " cntrl ": a control character other than a tab"; exit 2 }
            if (other) { print "line " other ": " k " set in a form this reader does not read"; exit 2 }
            if (found && !firstok) { print firstwhy; exit 2 }
            if (found) print first
        }
    ' ${SYNC_CONF}
}
conf_value() {
    local v
    v=$(conf_get "$1"); case $? in 2) echo "cloud_migrate_layout: ${SYNC_CONF}: ${v}" >&2; return 2 ;; esac
    printf '%s\n' "${v}"
}

# One folder, one spelling (the audit of the fix round, PL-001). The guards
# in main that decide whether a tier has already landed compared the conf's
# raw string with /ROCKNIX/Saves, so SAVES_REMOTE="/ROCKNIX/Saves/" -- a
# trailing slash, from a hand edit or an older setup -- read as the old
# layout: --check offered the move, and --apply copied the saves onto
# themselves (rclone's copy of a folder onto itself exits 0 and changes
# nothing), checked them clean against themselves, and deleted every file
# it had listed; the content folder went the same way. So a pointer is read
# as the folder it names:
#
#   clean_path     runs of / as one, no "." component, no trailing /; a
#                  leading / kept only if it had one, so the path handed to
#                  rclone is the one the other scripts use; it fails on a
#                  ".." component, which rclone resolves by rules of its
#                  own, so main leaves such a layout alone;
#   folder_key     that from the root, in one case when the cloud folds case
#                  (Dropbox, OneDrive) or cannot say whether it does;
#   same_folder    two keys equal;
#   inside_folder  the first strictly under the second, and rel_inside the
#                  part below, in the first one's own spelling.
CASE_INSENSITIVE=1
clean_path() { # <path>
    local p="$1" lead="" out="" part
    local -a parts=()
    case "${p}" in /*) lead="/" ;; esac
    IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "${p}"
    for part in "${parts[@]}"; do
        case "${part}" in
            ""|.) ;;
            ..) return 1 ;;
            *) out="${out:+${out}/}${part}" ;;
        esac
    done
    printf '%s%s' "${lead}" "${out}"
}
folder_abs() { # <cleaned path>: the same folder from the root, in its own spelling
    printf '/%s' "${1#/}"
}
folder_key() { # <path>
    local p
    p=$(clean_path "$1") || p="$1"
    p="/${p#/}"
    [ "${CASE_INSENSITIVE}" = 1 ] && p="${p,,}"
    printf '%s' "${p}"
}
same_folder() { # <path> <path>
    [ "$(folder_key "$1")" = "$(folder_key "$2")" ]
}
inside_folder() { # <path> <path>: the first strictly under the second
    local ka kb
    ka=$(folder_key "$1"); kb=$(folder_key "$2")
    [ "${ka}" != "${kb}" ] || return 1
    [ "${kb}" = "/" ] && return 0
    case "${ka}" in "${kb}"/*) return 0 ;; esac
    return 1
}
rel_inside() { # <path> <path>: the part of the first below the second (inside_folder holds)
    local a b
    a=$(clean_path "$1") || a="$1"; b=$(clean_path "$2") || b="$2"
    a=$(folder_abs "${a}"); b=$(folder_abs "${b}")
    if [ "${b}" = "/" ]; then printf '%s' "${a#/}"; else printf '%s' "${a:$(( ${#b} + 1 ))}"; fi
}

# A listing's bound (#143): three low-level retries, the value every other
# cloud script lists with.
readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)
# Every other call's (#308 claude F-CS-23): RCLONE_NET_OPTS from the conf,
# or the shipped value when the conf has none -- the bound the transfers
# carry everywhere else, where this script ran on rclone's own defaults
# (a 60 s connect, a 5 min idle, ten low-level retries, three runs: the
# behaviour #101 removed from every other script). Set in main.
RCLONE_NET_OPTS_FALLBACK="--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 10 --retries 1"
RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY=()
# What a verification compares by: size and hash where the remote keeps
# hashes, the bytes themselves where it keeps none (WebDAV, SFTP, SMB,
# FTP), where `rclone check` would otherwise compare sizes alone. Set in
# main from `rclone backend features`; a remote whose features cannot be
# read is checked by content too.
CHECK_OPTS=()

# One cloud transfer at a time (F-CS-23): the lock every other cloud script
# takes, for --apply only -- the check reads and writes nothing, as the
# match preview does. Without it a startup or game-exit sync could write
# into the folder this was moving. The same descriptor discipline as the
# others: the body runs with fd 9 closed, so nothing it starts holds the
# lock. Exit 75 is the skip EmulationStation names.
CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK=/var/run/cloud_sync.lock
take_cloud_lock() {
    local tries=0
    exec 9>"${CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK}"
    while ! flock -n 9; do
        if [ "${tries}" -ge 4 ]; then
            echo "Skipped: another cloud sync is already running. Try again when it's done."
            exit 75
        fi
        tries=$((tries + 1))
        sleep 0.25
    done
}

# A cloud that did not answer is not an empty cloud (audit #307 PL-027).
# Every presence test here used to be `[ -n "$(rclone lsf ... 2>/dev/null |
# head -1)" ]`, which discards rclone's exit: a listing that failed read as
# a folder with nothing in it, and --apply went on to rewrite the pointers
# with nothing copied. A listing now ends one of three ways: it listed
# (LISTING holds what it said, perhaps nothing), the folder is not there
# (rclone's 3/4, or the nearest listable parent lacks it -- #142's walk,
# for a server whose "missing" rclone does not map to 3), or the cloud
# could not be read -- and then the run stops where it is, saying so, with
# every pointer that has not already landed left where it was.
unreadable() { # <path> <rclone exit>
    local rc="$2"
    [ "${rc}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null || rc=1
    say "Couldn't read your cloud, so nothing more was changed. Try again when you're online."
    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "could not list $1 (rclone exit $2); stopped" 2>/dev/null
    exit "${rc}"
}

# Is this remote path missing, rather than unreadable? cloud_content_restore's
# walk, verbatim: up to the nearest level that lists; a level that lists and
# lacks the next name is a path not created yet (0), one that holds it means
# the failure was something else (1), and a root that will not list is
# broken (1).
absent_not_broken() {
    local path="${1%/}" remote rel name parent listing
    remote="${path%%:*}:"; rel="${path#*:}"; rel="${rel#/}"
    while [ -n "${rel}" ]; do
        name="${rel##*/}"; parent="${rel%/*}"
        [ "${parent}" = "${rel}" ] && parent=""
        if listing=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "${remote}/${parent:+${parent}/}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
            printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- "${name}/" && return 1
            return 0
        fi
        [ -n "${parent}" ] || return 1
        rel="${parent}"
    done
    return 1
}

# LISTING=what rclone lsf [args] <path> lists; nothing for a folder that is
# not there; the run stops for one that cannot be read. Never called inside
# $(...), so the stop is the script's.
LISTING=""
list_or_stop() { # <path> [lsf args...]
    local path="$1" rc
    shift
    LISTING=$(rclone lsf "$@" "${path}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
    case "${rc}" in
        0) return 0 ;;
        3|4) LISTING=""; return 0 ;;
    esac
    if absent_not_broken "${path}"; then
        LISTING=""
        return 0
    fi
    unreadable "${path}" "${rc}"
}

# Does a remote path exist and hold anything?
has_entries() {
    list_or_stop "$1"
    [ -n "${LISTING}" ]
}

# Does it hold actual files, ignoring the backup folder underneath it?
#
# Not the same question as "is it empty". The original layout has the backups
# nested inside the saves folder, so a saves folder with nothing in it but
# that subdirectory still lists an entry -- and reading that as "the saves are
# here" would move the backups into the middle of the saves.
#
# The same exclusions are what the saves relocation carries (audit #307
# PL-025): a test that looks past backup/ and Backups/ and a copy that then
# moves them is how the original layout's settings archives landed in
# Saves/backup/. Anchored at the folder's root, where the nested layout put
# them; the caller adds the tiers nested deeper. Every argument is passed
# as it is given -- the exclusion used to travel as one unquoted word
# (${extra}), which the shell split and glob-expanded against the working
# directory (#308 claude F-CS-23).
SAVES_EXCLUDES=(--exclude '/backup/**' --exclude '/Backups/**')
has_files() { # <path> [more lsf arguments...]
    local path="$1"
    shift
    # The setup note is not a save and must not outrank another root's data.
    list_or_stop "${path}" --files-only -R "${SAVES_EXCLUDES[@]}" --exclude '/README.txt' "$@"
    [ -n "${LISTING}" ]
}

# Does a remote path exist?
#
# NOT `rclone lsjson --stat`, which is what this used to be. On bucket-based
# remotes (S3, B2, Minio) stat synthesises a directory entry for *any* path --
# verified against Minio on rclone 1.60 and 1.74, where
# "utterly-bogus-never-created" reports success with IsDir true. So it can
# never report absence there, and every caller that branched on it took the
# "exists" path unconditionally.
#
# A listing can report absence. Two questions, because a directory can be real
# without holding files: does it contain anything, or does its parent list it
# (which is what an --s3-directory-markers marker object produces)?
exists() {
    list_or_stop "$1"
    [ -n "${LISTING}" ] && return 0
    local parent name
    parent="${1%/}"; name="${parent##*/}"; parent="${parent%/*}"
    [ -n "${name}" ] || return 1
    list_or_stop "${parent}/" --dirs-only
    printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | grep -qxF -- "${name}/"
}

# Did a `rclone check` find the two sides the same? Only when it says so
# both ways: its exit status is 0, and its count of differences is exactly
# zero. The count alone was the test here, as a substring -- and "10
# differences found" contains "0 differences found", so a check that found
# ten changed files let the pointer move and the old folder go, and a new
# folder holding ten other versions of the same names read as a partial
# copy to resume into (the audit of the fixes to #307, G-A-01).
check_clean() { # <rclone check's exit status> <its output>
    [ "$1" -eq 0 ] 2>/dev/null || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "$2" | grep -qE '(^|[^0-9])0 differences found'
}

# Relocate a folder by copy, verify, delete -- never `rclone move`.
#
# move deletes as it goes, so an interruption -- a handheld dropping off wifi is
# the normal case, not the exception -- leaves the library split across two
# paths with no record of which files went where (#57, upgrade-and-install.md).
# Copy first: a second run finds the copied files already present and skips
# them. Verify by content with `rclone check`, reading its whole output rather
# than one line of it (engineering-practices.md: rclone prints "N matching
# files" last, and a check against the last line matched nothing). Only a
# verified pass removes the source; a failed one leaves both sides intact and
# says so.
#
# Pipelines are avoided on purpose: `rclone ... | tail` reports tail's status,
# which is how a short backup once announced itself a success.
#
# The tier's pointer is written the moment its copy is verified, before its
# source is removed (audit #307 PL-026). Both pointers used to be written
# after both moves, so a run that moved the saves and was cut before the
# end left SAVES_REMOTE at the emptied folder -- a device syncing to a
# folder with nothing in it -- and the next run, finding the new folder
# already there, refused it. Now a cut run leaves each tier either where it
# was (not yet verified) or where it went (pointer written), and the next
# run moves only what has not landed.
#
# Any filter arguments after the fourth are the tier's own (PL-025): they
# decide which files are the tier's, so a folder nested in the source that
# belongs to another tier -- the original layout's backup/ and Content/
# inside the saves folder -- is neither moved with it nor deleted with it.
#
# And the source loses only what was copied and verified (audit #307
# PL-053). The files are listed once, by those filters, and the list is the
# whole job: the copy, the check and the deletion each take exactly it
# (--files-from-raw, which keeps a name's spaces), and the empty folders go
# after. The old folder used to be purged after a point-in-time check, so a
# save another device wrote into it between the check and the purge was
# lost; now it is not on the list, stays where it was written, and is
# still there for that device's own migration.
#
# 0 when the tier moved; 1 when its copy or check failed, the old folder
# whole; 2 when its pointer could not be written, which set_pointer has
# said, the old folder whole too.
# The second device's move, onto a current folder the fleet already made
# (RELOCATE_MERGE=1, D-CLOUD-168): the first device's move made the folder
# and removed the old one, and a device still on the old build then wrote
# its saves back under the old name (the mixed-installation test, step 3),
# so when it upgrades its old folder holds files and the new one exists.
# Refusing would strand it on NOT NOW for ever; merging is the sync's own
# rule -- the newer copy of each file wins -- made non-destructive: every
# version that differs between the two folders is set aside first, under
# the same <saves>-replaced/<stamp> shelf the backup keeps its conflict
# losers on, then the copy runs with --update and the new folder's own
# overwritten copies go to that shelf too (--backup-dir), and the old
# folder is removed only once every name it held is present in the new
# one. Nothing in the new folder is deleted, and nothing is lost: each
# byte that was in the cloud is in the new folder or on the shelf.
RELOCATE_MERGE=0
merge_shelf() { # <dst>: the set-aside beside the destination, one folder per run
    echo "${1%/}-replaced/$(date +%Y_%m_%d-%H%M%S)-move"
}

relocate() { # <src> <dst> <what> <pointer key> [filter arguments...]
    local src="$1" dst="$2" what="$3" key="$4" out list
    shift 4
    local -a filt=("$@")
    # One folder under two spellings is not a move (PL-001): copied onto
    # itself it checks clean, and the delete after it removes every file
    # it listed. Refused here whatever the caller compared.
    if same_folder "${src#*:}" "${dst#*:}"; then
        say "REFUSING: ${src} and ${dst} are the same folder, so nothing was copied or removed."
        logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "relocate: ${src} and ${dst} are one folder; refused" 2>/dev/null
        return 1
    fi
    # A destination inside the source -- a saves folder at /ROCKNIX moving
    # to /ROCKNIX/Saves -- is never listed as the source's own: a run cut
    # after its copy left part of it there, and the resume moved that copy
    # into /ROCKNIX/Saves/Saves (PL-001, found with the spelling cases).
    if inside_folder "${dst#*:}" "${src#*:}"; then
        filt+=(--exclude "/$(rel_inside "${dst#*:}" "${src#*:}")/**")
    fi
    list_or_stop "${src}" -R --files-only "${filt[@]}"
    if [ -z "${LISTING}" ]; then
        [ -z "${key}" ] || set_pointer "${key}" "${dst#*:}" || return 2
        return 0
    fi
    list=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_migrate_layout.XXXXXX) || { say "Couldn't make a working file on this device; nothing was moved."; return 1; }
    printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" > "${list}"
    if [ "${RELOCATE_MERGE}" = 1 ]; then
        merge_into "${src}" "${dst}" "${what}" "${key}" "${list}"
        return $?
    fi
    say "Copying ${what}..."
    # Under --apply the move runs on a page (GuiCloudTransfer, fork #353):
    # ">>> doing" names the step for its row 3, and the copy's own progress
    # goes to stdout for the page's counters (COPYING n OF m), as every
    # transfer's does; the check and the delete print nothing it reads.
    local copy_rc
    if [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ]; then
        echo ">>> doing copy"
        rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false --progress --stats 2s \
            "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${list}.out"; copy_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
        out=$(cat "${list}.out" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "${list}.out"
    else
        out=$(rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1); copy_rc=$?
    fi
    if [ "${copy_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${out}" | tail -3
        # A copy that stopped part-way has put some files in the new
        # folder; only the old one is as it was (G-A-12).
        say "Couldn't finish copying ${what}. Nothing was removed from the old folder; some files may already be in the new one."
        rm -f "${list}"
        return 1
    fi
    say "Verifying ${what}..."
    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing verify"
    out=$(rclone check "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --one-way "${CHECK_OPTS[@]}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1)
    if ! check_clean $? "${out}"; then
        printf '%s\n' "${out}" | grep -iE "differ|missing|error" | head -3
        say "The copy of ${what} didn't match, so nothing was removed from the old folder."
        rm -f "${list}"
        return 1
    fi
    # The source goes only once the pointer has landed (G-A-02): a pointer
    # that could not be written leaves the device on the old folder, so the
    # old folder must still hold everything -- the next run finds the copy
    # already there and resumes.
    # A folder with no pointer of its own (the set-aside beside the saves,
    # named from SAVES_REMOTE by the scripts) has nothing to record here.
    if [ -n "${key}" ] && ! set_pointer "${key}" "${dst#*:}"; then
        rm -f "${list}"
        return 2
    fi
    say "Removing the old ${what} folder..."
    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing remove"
    if ! rclone delete "${src}" --files-from-raw "${list}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        say "The verified copy is in the new folder, but the old files couldn't be removed. Try again to finish."
        rm -f "${list}"
        return 1
    fi
    rclone rmdirs "${src}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
    rm -f "${list}"
    return 0
}

# relocate's merge half (RELOCATE_MERGE, above): shelf, copy --update, verify
# by presence, remove. <list> is the source's own file listing.
merge_into() { # <src> <dst> <what> <pointer key> <list>
    local src="$1" dst="$2" what="$3" key="$4" list="$5" shelf differ missing out rc
    shelf="${dst%%:*}:$(merge_shelf "${dst#*:}")"
    differ=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_migrate_layout.XXXXXX) || { rm -f "${list}"; return 1; }
    missing="${differ}.missing"
    say "Merging ${what} into ${dst}: the newer copy of each file is kept, the other set aside under ${shelf#*:}."
    # 1. What differs between the two folders is shelved from the source
    #    first; the destination's own copies the update replaces follow
    #    through --backup-dir. A check that cannot run shelves nothing and
    #    stops here (guards fail closed).
    rclone check "${src}" "${dst}" --one-way --files-from-raw "${list}" --differ "${differ}" "${CHECK_OPTS[@]}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
    case "${rc}" in 0|1) ;; *)
        say "Couldn't compare ${what} with the new folder, so nothing was merged."
        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    if [ -s "${differ}" ]; then
        [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing copy"
        if ! out=$(rclone copy "${src}" "${shelf}" --files-from-raw "${differ}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1); then
            printf '%s\n' "${out}" | tail -3
            say "Couldn't set aside the ${what} that differ, so nothing was merged."
            rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1
        fi
        say "$(grep -c . "${differ}") ${what} file(s) differ between the folders; the old folder's copies are on the shelf."
    fi
    # 2. The copy, newer wins; a file the new folder had a newer copy of is
    #    left as it is, and one it replaces goes to the shelf.
    say "Copying ${what}..."
    local copy_rc
    if [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ]; then
        echo ">>> doing copy"
        rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --update --backup-dir "${shelf}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false --progress --stats 2s \
            "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${list}.out"; copy_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
        out=$(cat "${list}.out" 2>/dev/null); rm -f "${list}.out"
    else
        out=$(rclone copy "${src}" "${dst}" --files-from-raw "${list}" --update --backup-dir "${shelf}" --create-empty-src-dirs=false "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1); copy_rc=$?
    fi
    if [ "${copy_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${out}" | tail -3
        say "Couldn't finish merging ${what}. Nothing was removed from the old folder."
        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1
    fi
    # 3. Verified by presence: every name the old folder held is in the new
    #    one. Content may differ where the new folder's copy was newer, and
    #    that copy is the one kept, so a content check is not the test here.
    say "Verifying ${what}..."
    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing verify"
    : > "${missing}"
    rclone check "${src}" "${dst}" --one-way --files-from-raw "${list}" --missing-on-dst "${missing}" "${CHECK_OPTS[@]}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
    if [ "${rc}" -gt 1 ] || [ -s "${missing}" ]; then
        say "Not every ${what} file reached the new folder ($(grep -c . "${missing}" 2>/dev/null) missing), so nothing was removed from the old folder."
        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "${key}" ] && ! set_pointer "${key}" "${dst#*:}"; then
        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"; return 2
    fi
    say "Removing the old ${what} folder..."
    [ "${MODE}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> doing remove"
    if ! rclone delete "${src}" --files-from-raw "${list}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        say "The merged files are in the new folder, but the old files couldn't be removed. Try again to finish."
        rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"
        return 1
    fi
    rclone rmdirs "${src}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || :
    rm -f "${list}" "${differ}" "${missing}"
    return 0
}

# Point a key of the conf at a tier's new folder: the line rewritten in
# place, or added when the conf has none -- and then read back. A write
# that did not land (a full or read-only /storage, a path sed's
# replacement would mangle) is a failure the caller must stop on, before
# anything is removed (the audit of the fixes to #307, G-A-02): its result
# used to go unread, and relocate deleted the old folder after it either
# way, leaving the device pointed at a folder the run had just emptied.
# 0 when the conf now says <remote path>, 1 when it does not.
set_pointer() { # <key> <remote path>
    if grep -q "^$1=" "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null; then
        sed -i "s|^$1=.*|$1=\"$2\"|" "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null
    else
        printf '%s="%s"\n' "$1" "$2" >> "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null
    fi
    if [ "$(conf_value "$1")" != "$2" ]; then
        say "Couldn't save the new folder in this device's settings. It still uses the old one, and nothing was removed from it."
        echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE SAVED"
        logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "could not write $1 to ${SYNC_CONF}; stopped before removing anything" 2>/dev/null
        return 1
    fi
    say "Now using ${2:-the root of your cloud} for your $(tier_words "$1")."
}

# Pointer-only transitions describe one layout. Stage every change beside the
# config, then publish it with one rename: failure at any write keeps the old
# selection intact and a retry still sees the original transition (#471 PL-002).
# Real copy/move steps keep their per-tier verified publication and recovery
# record; they must not point at a destination before its copy is complete.
set_pointers() { # <key> <path> [<key> <path> ...]
    local tmp target="${SYNC_CONF}" rc=1
    tmp=$(mktemp "${SYNC_CONF}.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || tmp=""
    if [ -n "${tmp}" ] && [ -f "${target}" ] && cp -p "${target}" "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null; then
        (
            SYNC_CONF="${tmp}"
            while [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; do
                set_pointer "$1" "$2" >/dev/null || exit 1
                shift 2
            done
        ) && mv -f "${tmp}" "${target}" 2>/dev/null && rc=0
    fi
    if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
        [ -z "${tmp}" ] || rm -f "${tmp}"
        say "Couldn't save the new folders in this device's settings. Its previous folder choices are unchanged."
        echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE SAVED"
        return 1
    fi
    while [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; do
        say "Now using ${2:-the root of your cloud} for your $(tier_words "$1")."
        shift 2
    done
}

# A tier as the player knows it (es-player-text.md: the four tiers), for
# the tidy page's lines -- which named the config key (audit of the fixes,
# claude G-A-11).
tier_words() { # <pointer key>
    case "$1" in
        SAVES_REMOTE) echo "saves" ;;
        SETTINGS_REMOTE) echo "settings backups" ;;
        CONTENT_REMOTE) echo "ROMs, BIOS, and game content" ;;
        *) echo "files" ;;
    esac
}

# Is an existing destination a partial copy of this source, and nothing else?
#
# The refusals below exist so two devices' libraries are never merged. But a
# copy interrupted half-way also leaves a destination that exists, and the same
# refusal would then block the resume forever. The two cases differ in one
# checkable way: a partial copy holds nothing that did not come from the
# source. The reverse one-way check asks exactly that -- every file in dst is
# present and identical in src -- so a foreign file in dst fails it and the
# refusal stands.
resumable() {
    local src="$1" dst="$2" out
    out=$(rclone check "${dst}" "${src}" --one-way "${CHECK_OPTS[@]}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>&1)
    check_clean $? "${out}" && return 0
    # The equality check handles a subset of completed files, but a killed
    # upload can also leave one file truncated (#479). Only the original,
    # validated recovery record permits checking that case. Every destination
    # name must exist in the source, and every byte must match its prefix;
    # neither a record alone nor a smaller size authorizes a foreign merge.
    [ "${MIGRATION_RESUMING}" = 1 ] || return 1
    local source_files destination_files rows row name size source_hash destination_hash
    source_files=$(rclone lsjson "${src}" --recursive --files-only "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    destination_files=$(rclone lsjson "${dst}" --recursive --files-only "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    rows=$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "${source_files}" "${destination_files}" | jq -cer -s '
        def valid:
          type=="array" and all(.[];
            (.Path | type=="string" and length>0 and
              (explode | all(.[]; .>=32)) and
              (split("/") | all(.[]; .!="" and .!="." and .!=".."))) and
            (.Size | type=="number" and .>=0 and floor==.)) and
          ((map(.Path) | unique | length)==length);
        if length!=2 or (all(.[]; valid) | not) then error("invalid file listing") else . end |
        (reduce .[0][] as $file ({}; .[$file.Path]=$file.Size)) as $source |
        .[1] |
        if length==0 or
           (all(.[]; $source[.Path]!=null and .Size<=$source[.Path]) | not) or
           (any(.[]; .Size<$source[.Path]) | not)
        then error("not a truncated subset")
        else .[] | [.Path,.Size] | @base64 end') || return 1
    while IFS= read -r row; do
        row=$(printf '%s' "${row}" | base64 -d) || return 1
        name=$(printf '%s' "${row}" | jq -r '.[0]') || return 1
        size=$(printf '%s' "${row}" | jq -r '.[1]') || return 1
        # pipefail is local to each subshell: a failed provider read
        # must never become the successful hash of an empty stream.
        destination_hash=$(set -o pipefail; rclone cat "${dst%/}/${name}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sha256sum) || return 1
        source_hash=$(set -o pipefail; rclone cat "${src%/}/${name}" --count "${size}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sha256sum) || return 1
        [ "${source_hash}" = "${destination_hash}" ] || return 1
    done <<< "${rows}"
    return 0
}

# What cloud_sync_helper would have derived CONTENT_REMOTE to be for a given
# SAVES_REMOTE. The helper deliberately derives it rather than taking the shipped
# default, so that ROMs and saves stay in one namespace -- its own comment
# calls a split "worse than either layout alone".
#
# That is exactly what this script used to produce: it moved saves and backups
# to /ROCKNIX and left CONTENT_REMOTE behind, so a migrated device looked for its
# ROMs under a /GAMES that no longer had anything in it. Matching against the
# derived value is how we tell our own pointer from one the owner chose --
# theirs is left alone.
derived_content() {
    local sync="$1" parent
    parent=$(dirname "${sync}")
    [ "${parent}" = "/" ] && parent="${sync}"
    echo "${parent%/}/Content"
}

# RC2 could finish its saves/backups moves before /GAMES/Content; run101
# could finish both pointers before its discarded/content tiers (#391).
# Only these exact earlier defaults are inherited derived content. A custom
# path ending in /Content is still the player's independent choice.
historical_content() {
    same_folder "$1" /GAMES/Content || same_folder "$1" /ROCKNIX/Content
}

moving_content() { # <saves source> <content pointer>
    [ -n "$2" ] && ! same_folder "$2" "${NEW_CONTENT}" || return 1
    same_folder "$2" "$(derived_content "$(folder_abs "$1")")" && return 0
    { superseded_default "$1" || same_folder "$1" "${NEW_SAVES}"; } && historical_content "$2"
}

# Move content to the current namespace if it is safe to, and repoint the
# config. Never merges into an existing destination -- that is the same
# interruptible half-migrated state the saves move refuses.
migrate_content() {
    local remote="$1" content="$2" mode="$3"

    if has_entries "${remote}${content}/"; then
        if exists "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}" && ! resumable "${remote}${content}" "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}"; then
            if fleet_made "${remote}"; then
                RELOCATE_MERGE=1   # the fleet's folder: the second device's content merges (D-CLOUD-168)
            else
                say "REFUSING: ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT} already exists, and ${remote}${content}"
                say "holds files. Nothing moved and the config is unchanged -- merging two"
                say "content folders is not something to do without being asked."
                [ "${mode}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> why THE NEW FOLDER ALREADY HAS FILES IN IT"
                return 4
            fi
        fi
        say "Would copy, verify, then remove  ${remote}${content}  ->  ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}"
        if [ "${mode}" != "--apply" ]; then
            echo ">>> plan content ${NEW_ROOT}"
            say "Nothing has been changed. Run with --apply to do it."
            return 0
        fi
        local rrc=0
        relocate "${remote}${content}" "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}" "content" CONTENT_REMOTE || rrc=$?
        if [ "${rrc}" -ne 0 ]; then
            # 2 is a pointer that could not be written, which has said so.
            if [ "${rrc}" -ne 2 ]; then
                say "The config is unchanged."
                echo ">>> why SOME FILES DIDN'T FINISH"
            fi
            return 5
        fi
        say "Content is now at ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}."
        return 0
    else
        say "Nothing is stored at ${remote}${content}, so only the setting changes."
        if [ "${mode}" != "--apply" ]; then
            echo ">>> plan none ${NEW_ROOT}"
            say "Nothing has been changed. Run with --apply to do it."
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    set_pointer CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEW_CONTENT}" || return 5
    say "Content is now at ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}."
    return 0
}

# --- the layout as facts (#353, #356) -----------------------------------
#
# One line per fact and nothing the interface has to parse out of prose:
#
#   STATE=current               the saves folder is the current default
#   STATE=kept                  a superseded default this device chose to keep (--keep)
#   STATE=superseded-with-files a default this project once shipped, holding saves:
#                               the move is offered (D-CLOUD-160)
#   STATE=superseded-empty      such a default with nothing in it, or absent:
#                               the creation of the current layout is offered (D-CLOUD-161)
#   STATE=own                   a folder the player chose; nothing is offered
#   CURRENT_EXISTS=0|1          whether the current default's saves folder lists
#   MARKER=layout=<n> | -       the cloud's marker, when one is there
# An unrecorded old shelf can be an interrupted predecessor's, or a sibling's
# live history. If saves still live at the earlier root, leave its shelf there.
# A retained migration record identifies its own source independently and does
# not use this inference. Failed listings still stop through has_files/entries.
inherited_discarded() { # <remote>; sets RECOVERY_DISCARDED and RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL
    local remote="$1" earlier
    RECOVERY_DISCARDED=""
    RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL=()
    for earlier in "${SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]}"; do
        has_entries "${remote}${earlier}-replaced/" || continue
        if [ "${earlier}" = /GAMES ]; then
            # The old root nests settings/content beside the actual saves.
            has_files "${remote}${earlier}/" --exclude '/backup/**' \
                --exclude '/Content/**' --exclude '/README.txt' && continue
        else
            has_files "${remote}${earlier}/" --exclude '/README.txt' && continue
        fi
        RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL+=("${earlier}-replaced")
    done
    [ "${#RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL[@]}" -gt 0 ] || return 1
    RECOVERY_DISCARDED="${RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL[0]}"
    return 0
}

layout_state() { # <remote> <saves> <backups> <content>
    local remote="$1" saves="$2" backups="$3" content="$4" state keep cur=0 marker old_replaced=""
    if [ -e "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" ]; then
        migration_record_load "${remote}" || return $?
        printf 'STATE=migration-pending\nSOURCE=%s\nCURRENT=%s\n' "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"
        return 0
    fi
    keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || return 2
    echo "SAVES=${saves}"
    echo "BACKUPS=${backups}"
    echo "CONTENT=${content}"
    echo "CURRENT=${NEW_SAVES}"
    # The folder this device is configured for is one witness; the cloud is
    # the other. A device upgraded from stock carries /GAMES in its conf
    # while its saves sit in /ROCKNIX/Saves, made by its sibling on the
    # fork's earlier build (the Retroid Pocket Nova, 2026-10-01): read from
    # the conf alone it is "superseded, empty" and would be offered a fresh
    # /pixelelated beside its real saves. So every default this project
    # once shipped is looked at, and the one holding files is the source
    # the move is offered from (SOURCE=), the configured one or not.
    local source=""
    if same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then
        state=current
        # Older builds wrote no recovery record. Their current primary
        # pointers do not prove the derived content or discarded shelf moved.
        # This is a folder-page read, never an extra probe on a direct sync.
        if same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"; then
            if historical_content "${content}"; then
                state=migration-pending
            else
                inherited_discarded "${remote}" && state=migration-pending
            fi
        fi
    elif [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}"; then
        state=kept
    elif superseded_default "${saves}"; then
        superseded_source "${remote}" "${saves}"; source="${SOURCE_FOUND}"
        if [ -n "${source}" ]; then state=superseded-with-files; else state=superseded-empty; fi
    else
        state=own
    fi
    echo "SOURCE=${source:--}"
    exists "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}" && cur=1
    echo "CURRENT_EXISTS=${cur}"
    marker=$(rclone cat "${remote}${NEW_SAVES%/*}/${LAYOUT_MARKER}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -cd 'a-z0-9=')
    echo "MARKER=${marker:--}"
    echo "STATE=${state}"
    return 0
}

# KEEP USING <folder>: asked once (D-CLOUD-160). The conf remembers the
# folder kept, so --state reads "kept" until the folder changes.
layout_keep() { # <saves>
    set_pointer LAYOUT_KEEP "$1" || return 1
    say "Keeping ${1}; the move will not be offered again for this folder."
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "layout kept at $1 by request" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

# "Your other devices will follow": a device on a superseded default whose
# current-default folder already exists in the cloud -- another device made
# the move -- is re-pointed with no question and one line in the journal.
# Nothing is copied or removed here; the folders are already where they
# belong. 0 when the device now points at the current layout, 3 when there
# was nothing to follow, 1 when the conf could not be written.
layout_follow() { # <remote> <saves> <backups> <content>
    local remote="$1" saves="$2" backups="$3" content="$4" keep
    same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" && return 3
    superseded_default "${saves}" || return 3
    keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || return 2
    [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}" && return 3
    # One listing for the usual answer, "no device has moved yet": the
    # current folder's parent, which names Saves/ once it exists (exists()
    # would list the folder and then its parent, two rclone starts).
    list_or_stop "${remote}${NEW_SAVES%/*}/" --dirs-only
    printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | grep -qxF -- "${NEW_SAVES##*/}/" || return 3
    # A device whose old folder still holds files is not followed: they
    # would be stranded in a folder nothing reads once the pointer moves
    # (the futro's pre-mortem, 2026-10-01). The move is offered instead,
    # which copies, verifies and only then removes.
    has_files "${remote}${saves}/" && return 3
    backup_pointer_for "${remote}" "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"
    local -a pointers=(SAVES_REMOTE "${NEW_SAVES}" SETTINGS_REMOTE "${NEXT_BACKUPS}")
    # Content follows only where it was derived from the old folder or
    # never set; a folder the player chose for ROMs stays theirs.
    if content_unset || same_folder "${content}" "$(derived_content "$(folder_abs "${saves}")")" \
       || same_folder "${content}" "${saves%/}/Content"; then
        pointers+=(CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEW_CONTENT}")
    fi
    set_pointers "${pointers[@]}" || return 1
    say "Followed: this device now uses ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}, which another device already made."
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "followed the fleet from ${saves} to ${NEW_SAVES}" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

# A fresh install beside a fleet still on the earlier folder: this device
# is on the current default, the current saves folder holds no saves (it
# is not there, or only the seeding's folders and README are), and a
# folder this project once shipped as its default does hold them. Without
# this the device was offered CREATE IT beside the player's saves, and saw
# none of them on its first restore -- the mixed-installation test's fresh
# device (D-CLOUD-158). It is pointed at the earlier folder's layout -- a
# setting, nothing copied -- so it reads and writes where the saves are,
# and is then offered the move as every device on that folder is
# (D-CLOUD-160). 0 when it joined, 3 when there was nothing to join, 1
# when the conf could not be written.
layout_join() { # <remote> <saves> <content>
    local remote="$1" saves="$2" content="$3" keep
    if same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then
        has_files "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}/" --exclude '/README.txt' && return 3
    elif superseded_default "${saves}"; then
        # The Nova's shape (2026-09-30): a carried /GAMES with nothing in it,
        # the saves in /ROCKNIX/Saves beside it. Joined, the move is offered
        # from the folder that holds them and KEEP USING keeps that folder;
        # left on /GAMES, KEEP USING /ROCKNIX recorded /GAMES.
        keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || return 2
        [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}" && return 3
        has_files "${remote}${saves}/" && return 3
    else
        return 3
    fi
    earlier_source "${remote}" "${saves}" || return 3
    earlier_layout "${SOURCE_FOUND}" "${content}"
    local backups
    backups=$(conf_value SETTINGS_REMOTE) || return 2
    backup_pointer_for "${remote}" "${backups}" "${E_BACKUPS}"
    set_pointers SAVES_REMOTE "${E_SAVES}" SETTINGS_REMOTE "${NEXT_BACKUPS}" \
        CONTENT_REMOTE "${E_CONTENT}" || return 1
    say "Joined: this device now uses ${remote}${E_SAVES}, where your saves already are."
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "joined the fleet at ${E_SAVES}: no saves in ${NEW_SAVES}" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

# The wizard's seeding step (cloud_setup --seed-folders): join the earlier
# folder that holds the saves; else a device still on a default this
# project once shipped, with nothing in it and nothing anywhere, is on no
# folder at all (D-CLOUD-161) and is pointed at the current folders, which
# the seeding then makes and lists, as it does for any new cloud. Seeding
# the carried /GAMES itself put a README there, which every later check
# read as saves: the move was offered from /GAMES and left the player's
# saves in /ROCKNIX (2026-10-01). 0 when the device was pointed somewhere,
# 3 when its folder stands.
layout_settle() { # <remote> <saves> <backups> <content>
    local remote="$1" saves="$2" backups="$3" content="$4" rc keep
    layout_join "${remote}" "${saves}" "${content}"; rc=$?
    [ "${rc}" -ne 3 ] && return "${rc}"
    superseded_default "${saves}" || return 3
    keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || return 2
    [ -n "${keep}" ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${keep}" && return 3
    has_files "${remote}${saves}/" && return 3
    backup_pointer_for "${remote}" "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"
    local -a pointers=(SAVES_REMOTE "${NEW_SAVES}" SETTINGS_REMOTE "${NEXT_BACKUPS}")
    if content_unset || same_folder "${content}" "$(derived_content "$(folder_abs "${saves}")")" \
       || same_folder "${content}" "${saves%/}/Content"; then
        pointers+=(CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEW_CONTENT}")
    fi
    set_pointers "${pointers[@]}" || return 1
    say "Your cloud had nothing in ${remote}${saves}; this device now uses ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}."
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "settled a carried ${saves} with nothing in it on ${NEW_SAVES}" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

# Did another device of ours make the current layout? The marker at the
# folder's parent says so (write_marker, after a move or a seeding). A
# current folder with no marker is somebody's own folder of the same name,
# which the refusals below still protect.
fleet_made() { # <remote>
    [ "${REMOTE_LAYOUT}" = "${LAYOUT_VERSION}" ]
}

# A marker is a version, not merely a prefix. Validate its complete bytes;
# shell substitution would silently discard NULs and trailing newlines. A
# failed read is not absence if the parent still lists the marker.
read_marker() { # <remote>
    local tmp rc version
    REMOTE_LAYOUT=0
    tmp=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud_layout_marker.XXXXXX) || return 5
    rclone cat "${1}${NEW_ROOT}/${LAYOUT_MARKER}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" > "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
    if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
        rm -f "${tmp}"
        list_or_stop "${1}${NEW_ROOT}/" --files-only
        if printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | grep -qFx -- "${LAYOUT_MARKER}"; then
            unreadable "${1}${NEW_ROOT}/${LAYOUT_MARKER}" "${rc}"
        fi
        return 0
    fi
    for version in 1 2; do
        if printf 'layout=%s\n' "${version}" | cmp -s - "${tmp}"; then
            REMOTE_LAYOUT="${version}"
            rm -f "${tmp}"
            return 0
        fi
    done
    rm -f "${tmp}"
    say "This cloud folder uses a layout this version can't read. No further changes were made. Check for a newer system version before trying again."
    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "unsupported or malformed layout marker; refused" 2>/dev/null
    return 4
}

write_marker() { # <remote>
    # Another device may have changed the marker while the tiers moved.
    read_marker "$1" || return $?
    if printf 'layout=%s\n' "${LAYOUT_VERSION}" | rclone rcat "${1}${NEW_SAVES%/*}/${LAYOUT_MARKER}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" 2>/dev/null; then
        read_marker "$1" || return $?
        [ "${REMOTE_LAYOUT}" = "${LAYOUT_VERSION}" ] || return 5
        return 0
    fi
    say "Your files moved, but the cloud folder setup didn't finish. Try the move again to finish it."
    echo ">>> why SOME FILES DIDN'T FINISH"
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "could not write ${LAYOUT_MARKER} at ${1}${NEW_SAVES%/*}" 2>/dev/null
    return 5
}

# Local recovery state keeps the sources after their live pointers advance.
# It is never sourced as shell and never grants permission to merge a foreign
# destination. Each retry still verifies the actual cloud bytes. A record is
# bound to the remote configuration and the original/current pointer choices.
remote_fingerprint() {
    # rclone refreshes OAuth tokens during ordinary transfers. Bind the
    # configured provider/root, not that routinely changing credential, file
    # comments, whitespace or field order. Let rclone parse its own syntax;
    # credentials pass only through memory to the digest, never into the record.
    local config
    if [ "${1:-}" = legacy ]; then
        # Existing schema1 records bind the old exact serialization. Accept
        # them only with that original binding, then upgrade on a saved stage.
        config=$(sed '/^[[:space:]]*token[[:space:]]*=/d' /storage/.config/rclone/rclone.conf) || return 1
    else
        config=$(rclone config dump 2>/dev/null) || return 1
        config=$(printf '%s\n' "${config}" | jq -ceS '
            if type=="object" and all(.[]; type=="object")
            then with_entries(.value |= del(.token)) else error("invalid config") end') || return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "${config}" | sha256sum
}

migration_record_save() {
    migration_record_write "$@" && return 0
    say "Couldn't save the cloud move's progress on this device. Try again when storage is available."
    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE SAVED"
    return 5
}

migration_record_write() { # <stage>; consumes the calling step's local paths
    local stage="$1" tmp fingerprint
    fingerprint=$(remote_fingerprint) || return 5
    fingerprint="${fingerprint%% *}"
    tmp=$(mktemp "${MIGRATION_RECORD}.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null) || return 5
    if [ "${MIGRATION_ACTIVE}" = 1 ]; then
        jq --arg stage "${stage}" --arg fingerprint "${fingerprint}" --arg discarded "${old_replaced}" \
            '.stage=$stage | .fingerprint=$fingerprint | .fingerprint_format="rclone-json-v1" | .source.discarded=$discarded' \
            "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" > "${tmp}"
    else
        jq -n --arg remote "${remote}" --arg fingerprint "${fingerprint}" \
            --arg saves "${saves}" --arg backups "${backups}" --arg content "${content}" \
            --arg discarded "${old_replaced}" \
            --arg cs "$(conf_value SAVES_REMOTE)" --arg cb "$(conf_value SETTINGS_REMOTE)" \
            --arg cc "$(conf_value CONTENT_REMOTE)" --arg stage "${stage}" \
            '{schema:1,step:1,from:1,to:2,remote:$remote,fingerprint:$fingerprint,fingerprint_format:"rclone-json-v1",
              source:{saves:$saves,backups:$backups,content:$content,discarded:$discarded},
              configured:{saves:$cs,backups:$cb,content:$cc},stage:$stage}' > "${tmp}"
    fi
    if [ "$?" -ne 0 ] || ! sync || ! mv -f "${tmp}" "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" || ! sync; then
        rm -f "${tmp}"
        return 5
    fi
    MIGRATION_ACTIVE=1
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "migration step=1 from=1 to=2 stage=${stage}" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

migration_record_load() { # <remote>; restores the calling step's source paths
    [ -e "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" ] || return 0
    local fingerprint format key live initial target value
    format=$(jq -r '.fingerprint_format // "legacy"' "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" 2>/dev/null) || format=invalid
    case "${format}" in
        legacy) fingerprint=$(remote_fingerprint legacy) || return 5 ;;
        rclone-json-v1) fingerprint=$(remote_fingerprint) || return 5 ;;
        *)
            say "The previous cloud move couldn't be read safely. Nothing more was changed."
            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
            return 5 ;;
    esac
    fingerprint="${fingerprint%% *}"
    if ! jq -e '
        .schema==1 and .step==1 and .from==1 and .to==2 and
        (.remote | type=="string") and (.fingerprint | type=="string") and
        ([.source.saves,.source.backups,.source.content,
          .configured.saves,.configured.backups,.configured.content] |
          all(.[]; type=="string" and (explode | all(.[]; .>=32)))) and
        ((.source | has("discarded") | not) or
          (.source.discarded | type=="string" and (explode | all(.[]; .>=32))))
        ' "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        say "The previous cloud move couldn't be read safely. Nothing more was changed."
        echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
        return 5
    fi
    if ! jq -e --arg remote "$1" --arg fingerprint "${fingerprint}" \
        '.remote==$remote and .fingerprint==$fingerprint' "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" >/dev/null; then
        say "The previous cloud move couldn't be read safely. Restore the cloud connection used to start it under MANAGE CLOUD STORAGE, then try the move again. All remaining copies have been kept."
        echo ">>> why THE PREVIOUS CLOUD MOVE NEEDS ITS ORIGINAL CONNECTION"
        return 5
    fi
    for key in saves backups content; do
        case "${key}" in
            saves) live=$(conf_value SAVES_REMOTE); target="${NEW_SAVES}" ;;
            backups) live=$(conf_value SETTINGS_REMOTE); target="${NEW_BACKUPS}" ;;
            content) live=$(conf_value CONTENT_REMOTE); target="${NEW_CONTENT}" ;;
        esac
        initial=$(jq -r --arg k "${key}" '.configured[$k]' "${MIGRATION_RECORD}") || return 5
        if ! same_folder "${live}" "${initial}" && ! same_folder "${live}" "${target}"; then
            say "Your cloud folder choices changed during the move. Nothing more was changed."
            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER CHOICES CHANGED DURING THE MOVE"
            return 5
        fi
        value=$(jq -r --arg k "${key}" '.source[$k]' "${MIGRATION_RECORD}") || return 5
        value=$(clean_path "${value}") || return 5
        printf -v "${key}" '%s' "${value}"
    done
    # Optional in schema1: records written before #391 derive this shelf
    # from their retained saves source. New records keep it independently,
    # so recovering an old shelf never reselects a live saves folder.
    value=$(jq -r '.source.discarded // (.source.saves | rtrimstr("/") + "-replaced")' "${MIGRATION_RECORD}") || return 5
    old_replaced=$(clean_path "${value}") || return 5
    # A record created by this invocation is not evidence of an earlier
    # interrupted copy. In particular, content moves after begin is saved.
    [ "${MIGRATION_ACTIVE}" = 1 ] || MIGRATION_RESUMING=1
    MIGRATION_ACTIVE=1
    logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "migration step=1 from=1 to=2 resume" 2>/dev/null
    return 0
}

MODE="--check"
main() {
    # Every pointer this tool reads must be readable by the shared grammar
    # before anything is compared or moved (the audit of the fixes, claude
    # G3-D-05): a value the reader cannot read ends the run with its why,
    # as cloud_setup ends, never as an empty pointer that reads as a folder.
    local _k _v
    for _k in SAVESPATH SETTINGS_BACKUPS SAVES_REMOTE SETTINGS_REMOTE CONTENT_REMOTE RCLONE_NET_OPTS; do
        _v=$(conf_get "${_k}"); case $? in 2) echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be read (${SYNC_CONF}: ${_v})." >&2; echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"; exit 2 ;; esac
    done
    local mode="${1:---check}"
    local remote saves backups content old_root
    MODE="${mode}"

    remote=$(remote_name)
    if [ -z "${remote}" ]; then
        say "No cloud remote is configured; nothing to migrate."
        return 1
    fi

    # The cloud answers before anything is asked of it (PL-027): a remote
    # that does not list at its root is unreadable, and nothing below --
    # a presence test, a pointer -- is reached.
    # Not for --follow, which an exit sync on a device still on an earlier
    # folder runs before every write: its own first listing stops the run on
    # a cloud that cannot be read, and the probe and the features query were
    # two of the four rclone starts it cost each time (time to play,
    # 2026-10-01). Nothing it writes depends on either.
    local probe_rc
    if [ "${mode}" != "--follow" ]; then
        rclone lsd "${remote}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; probe_rc=$?
        [ "${probe_rc}" -eq 0 ] || unreadable "${remote}" "${probe_rc}"
    fi

    local net_opts
    net_opts=$(conf_value RCLONE_NET_OPTS | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ //; s/ $//')
    [ -n "${net_opts}" ] || net_opts="${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_FALLBACK}"
    read -r -a RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY <<< "${net_opts}"
    # The query creates the remote, a round trip on most backends, so it
    # carries the listing bound like every other call here (audit of the
    # fixes, G-A-11/G-A-10); one that fails or times out reads as "no
    # hashes", the safe side.
    local features=""
    [ "${mode}" != "--follow" ] && features=$(rclone backend features "${remote}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' \t\n')
    case "${features}" in *'"Hashes":["'*) ;; *) CHECK_OPTS=(--download) ;; esac
    # And whether it keeps case apart (PL-001): only a cloud that says so
    # holds /rocknix/saves and /ROCKNIX/Saves as two folders. One that folds
    # case, or whose features cannot be read, holds them as one, and a
    # pointer spelled either way is the new folder, so nothing moves -- the
    # safe side, since the other side deletes a folder copied onto itself.
    case "${features}" in *'"CaseInsensitive":false'*) CASE_INSENSITIVE=0 ;; *) CASE_INSENSITIVE=1 ;; esac

    saves=$(conf_value SAVES_REMOTE)
    backups=$(conf_value SETTINGS_REMOTE)

    content=$(conf_value CONTENT_REMOTE)

    # Each pointer as the folder it names (PL-001): cleaned for the paths
    # below and compared by folder_key, never as a string. A ".." cannot be
    # read as one folder without the cloud's own rules -- rclone resolves
    # /ROCKNIX/Old/../Saves to /ROCKNIX/Saves -- so a layout holding one is
    # left exactly as it is.
    local ptr cleaned
    for ptr in saves backups content; do
        if ! cleaned=$(clean_path "${!ptr}"); then
            say "REFUSING: a folder in this device's cloud settings has .. in it, so it can't be told which folder it means. Nothing was changed."
            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"
            logger -t cloud_migrate_layout "a pointer has a .. component; nothing done" 2>/dev/null
            return 4
        fi
        printf -v "${ptr}" '%s' "${cleaned}"
    done

    # All default-layout transitions share the version boundary, including
    # seeding through --settle. A custom layout elsewhere is independent.
    if superseded_default "${saves}" || same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then
        read_marker "${remote}" || return $?
    fi

    # A layout the owner chose is current too. CHANGE CLOUD FOLDER writes the
    # settings and content folders as SIBLINGS of the saves folder -- the
    # parent's Backups and Content, or the folder's own when it sits at the
    # root -- and a device on /Custom/Saves, /Custom/Backups, /Custom/Content
    # has nothing to migrate. Until 2026-09-11 only the /ROCKNIX names counted
    # as current, so this check offered to move a deliberately chosen layout
    # back to the default one (#74). The nested first layout, backups INSIDE
    # the saves folder, is the only shape this tool exists to move.
    if [ -e "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" ]; then
        case "${mode}" in
            --join|--follow) return 3 ;; # The explicit retry owns the remaining move.
            --settle|--keep|--write-marker)
                migration_record_load "${remote}" || return $?
                say "The cloud folder move hasn't finished. Try the move again to finish it."
                echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER MOVE DIDN'T FINISH"
                return 5 ;;
        esac
    fi
    case "${mode}" in
        --state)  layout_state "${remote}" "${saves}" "${backups}" "${content}"; return $? ;;
        --keep)   layout_keep "${saves}"; return $? ;;
        --follow) layout_follow "${remote}" "${saves}" "${backups}" "${content}"; return $? ;;
        --join)   layout_join "${remote}" "${saves}" "${content}"; return $? ;;
        --settle) layout_settle "${remote}" "${saves}" "${backups}" "${content}"; return $? ;;
        --write-marker)
            # Seeding must not declare an unfinished local move complete.
            [ ! -e "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" ] || return 5
            same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" || return 3
            write_marker "${remote}"; return $? ;;
    esac

    # Step 1 is the supported predecessor (unmarked/layout 1) to layout 2.
    # A layout-2 fleet may still have an older device's files to move, so
    # marker 2 does not skip that device's step. Later versions must add an
    # explicit dispatcher entry; read_marker refuses them in this build.
    case "${REMOTE_LAYOUT}" in
        0|1|2) migration_step_1 "${remote}" "${saves}" "${backups}" "${content}" "${mode}" ;;
        *) return 4 ;;
    esac
}

migration_step_1() {
    local remote="$1" saves="$2" backups="$3" content="$4" mode="$5" old_replaced=""
    local recovery_depth="${6:-0}"
    migration_record_load "${remote}" || return $?

    local sabs sib_parent
    sabs=$(folder_abs "${saves}")
    sib_parent="${sabs%/*}"; [ -n "${sib_parent}" ] || sib_parent="${sabs}"
    # A superseded default is not a layout of the player's own, however
    # sibling-shaped: /ROCKNIX/Saves beside /ROCKNIX/Backups is the fork's
    # earlier default and is offered the move (D-CLOUD-160).
    if ! superseded_default "${saves}" \
       && ! same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" && same_folder "${backups}" "${sib_parent}/Backups"; then
        if content_unset || same_folder "${content}" "${sib_parent}/Content"; then
            say "Already on a sibling layout of your own (${saves}, ${backups}); nothing to move."
            return 3
        fi
    fi

    if [ "${MIGRATION_ACTIVE}" = 0 ] && same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" \
       && same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"; then
        # The live primary pointers are authoritative. Another device may
        # still write old saves/backups: only the retained content pointer
        # and an owned discarded shelf are eligible for this recovery.
        inherited_discarded "${remote}" && old_replaced="${RECOVERY_DISCARDED}"
        if [ -z "${old_replaced}" ] && ! moving_content "${saves}" "${content}"; then
            # An older build may have stopped just before publication. An
            # explicit apply finishes that marker without inventing a move
            # or rewriting equivalent pointer spellings (PL-001).
            if [ "${mode}" = "--apply" ] && [ "${REMOTE_LAYOUT}" != "${LAYOUT_VERSION}" ]; then
                write_marker "${remote}" || return $?
            fi
            say "Already on the current layout (${NEW_SAVES}, ${NEW_BACKUPS})."
            return 3
        fi
    fi

    # The move starts from the folder that holds the saves. A device whose
    # configured folder is a superseded default with nothing in it, while
    # another superseded default's folder holds files (the Nova: /GAMES in
    # the conf, /ROCKNIX/Saves in the cloud), is first pointed at that
    # folder -- a setting, nothing copied -- and then moved from it like
    # any other. Backups and content are taken as that layout's siblings
    # (or the nested /GAMES/backup for the first layout).
    if [ "${MIGRATION_ACTIVE}" = 0 ] && superseded_default "${saves}" && ! has_files "${remote}${saves}/"; then
        local src
        superseded_source "${remote}" "${saves}"; src="${SOURCE_FOUND}"
        if [ -n "${src}" ] && ! same_folder "${src}" "${saves}"; then
            say "Your saves are in ${remote}${src}, not in ${remote}${saves} as this device was set; moving from there."
            local src_parent="${src%/*}"; [ -n "${src_parent}" ] || src_parent="${src}"
            local src_backups="${src_parent}/Backups"
            [ "${src}" = "/GAMES" ] && src_backups="/GAMES/backup"
            backup_pointer_for "${remote}" "${backups}" "${src_backups}"
            # Select sources here; publish pointers only after verified
            # copies, with the recovery record already retained below.
            saves="${src}"
            backups="${NEXT_BACKUPS}"
            content_unset && content="${src_parent}/Content"
            sabs=$(folder_abs "${saves}")
            sib_parent="${sabs%/*}"; [ -n "${sib_parent}" ] || sib_parent="${sabs}"
        fi
    fi
    [ -n "${old_replaced}" ] || old_replaced="${sabs%/}-replaced"

    # RC2 moved /GAMES to /ROCKNIX but left /GAMES-replaced behind. Check
    # every eligible historical shelf before starting, including when this
    # device still selects ROCKNIX. A live earlier sibling remains excluded.
    local -a discarded_sources=("${old_replaced}")
    local discarded_source
    if inherited_discarded "${remote}"; then
        for discarded_source in "${RECOVERY_DISCARDED_ALL[@]}"; do
            same_folder "${discarded_source}" "${old_replaced}" || discarded_sources+=("${discarded_source}")
        done
        if ! has_entries "${remote}${old_replaced}/"; then
            old_replaced="${RECOVERY_DISCARDED}"
        fi
    fi

    say "This device stores:"
    say "  saves    ${remote}${saves}"
    say "  backups  ${remote}${backups}"
    say ""
    say "The current layout is:"
    say "  saves    ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}"
    say "  backups  ${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}"
    say ""

    # Where the saves actually are. Under the original layout SAVES_REMOTE was the
    # folder itself; a device whose owner has already tidied them into a
    # subfolder is the more useful case to handle, since that is what somebody
    # does after losing files to a mirror.
    local saves_src="${saves}" nested
    # "at the root" must not count the saves subfolder, or a recursive listing
    # finds the files inside it and concludes they were at the root all along
    # -- which would move the whole folder, backups included, into Saves. Nor
    # the other tiers nested in it: the content folder derived beside the
    # saves (/GAMES/Content) holds files, and read as "saves at the root" it
    # sent a tidied saves/ subfolder into Saves/saves/ (found by F-CS-23's
    # case, a gap in the PL-025 commit).
    local -a root_nested=()
    for nested in "${backups}" "${content}"; do
        [ -n "${nested}" ] && inside_folder "${nested}" "${saves}" \
            && root_nested+=(--exclude "/$(rel_inside "${nested}" "${saves}")/**")
    done
    if ! has_files "${remote}${saves}/" --exclude '/saves/**' "${root_nested[@]}" \
       && has_files "${remote}${saves}/saves/"; then
        saves_src="${saves%/}/saves"
        say "Saves are in ${remote}${saves_src}, not at the root."
    fi
    # The other tiers nested inside the saves source ride with neither its
    # presence test nor its move (PL-025): the settings folder of the
    # original layout (/GAMES/backup) and the content folder derived beside
    # the saves (/GAMES/Content) each move to a place of their own.
    for nested in "${backups}" "${content}"; do
        [ -n "${nested}" ] && inside_folder "${nested}" "${saves_src}" \
            && SAVES_EXCLUDES+=(--exclude "/$(rel_inside "${nested}" "${saves_src}")/**")
    done

    # Refuse to move onto something already there. A move into an existing
    # directory is done file by file, which is exactly the interruptible,
    # half-migrated state worth avoiding -- and it could merge two devices'
    # libraries without anyone asking for that.
    #
    # Each tier is judged against its own source (PL-026): the backups
    # destination used to be compared with the saves source, so a copy of
    # the backups cut half-way could never be resumed. A tier whose pointer
    # already names the new folder has landed, and is left alone; one whose
    # source holds nothing has nothing to merge, and only its pointer moves --
    # the state an earlier build left when it was cut after its moves and
    # before its pointers.
    # Unless the fleet made the new folder (its marker, D-CLOUD-168): then
    # this is the second device's move and the tiers merge (merge_into).
    local blocked=0 merging=0
    if ! same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}" && has_entries "${remote}${backups}/" \
       && exists "${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}" \
       && ! resumable "${remote}${backups}" "${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}"; then
        if fleet_made "${remote}"; then merging=1; else
            say "REFUSING: ${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS} already exists."
            blocked=1
        fi
    fi
    if ! same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" && has_files "${remote}${saves_src}/" \
       && exists "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}" \
       && ! resumable "${remote}${saves_src}" "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}"; then
        if fleet_made "${remote}"; then merging=1; else
            say "REFUSING: ${remote}${NEW_SAVES} already exists."
            blocked=1
        fi
    fi
    for discarded_source in "${discarded_sources[@]}"; do
        if ! same_folder "${discarded_source}" "${NEW_SAVES}-replaced" && has_entries "${remote}${discarded_source}/" \
           && exists "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}-replaced" \
           && ! resumable "${remote}${discarded_source}" "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}-replaced"; then
            if fleet_made "${remote}"; then merging=1; else
                say "REFUSING: ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}-replaced already exists."
                blocked=1
            fi
        fi
    done
    # Check content before creating a recovery record or advancing any tier.
    # Otherwise a refusal could create the very record that a later retry
    # mistakes for an interrupted copy of that pre-existing destination.
    if moving_content "${saves}" "${content}" && has_entries "${remote}${content}/" \
       && exists "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}" \
       && ! resumable "${remote}${content}" "${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}"; then
        if fleet_made "${remote}"; then merging=1; else
            say "REFUSING: ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT} already exists."
            blocked=1
        fi
    fi
    if [ "${blocked}" = "1" ]; then
        [ "${mode}" = "--apply" ] && echo ">>> why THE NEW FOLDER ALREADY HAS FILES IN IT"
        return 4
    fi
    if [ "${merging}" = 1 ]; then
        say "Another device has already moved to ${remote}${NEW_SAVES%/*}: this one's folders merge into it, the newer copy of each file kept and the other set aside."
        RELOCATE_MERGE=1
    fi

    say "Would move, server-side, leaving anything else where it is:"
    local plan=""
    if ! same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}" && has_entries "${remote}${backups}/"; then
        say "  ${remote}${backups}  ->  ${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}"; plan="${plan:+${plan},}backups"
    fi
    if ! same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" && has_files "${remote}${saves_src}/"; then
        say "  ${remote}${saves_src}  ->  ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}"; plan="${plan:+${plan},}saves"
    fi
    # The set-aside of conflict losers beside the saves folder
    # (<saves>-replaced, cloud_backup's) is ours and travels with the saves
    # (D-CLOUD-165): to a player the change is a renamed shelf, not a new
    # one, and nothing of ours stays under the old name.
    local discarded_planned=0
    for discarded_source in "${discarded_sources[@]}"; do
        if ! same_folder "${discarded_source}" "${NEW_SAVES}-replaced" && has_entries "${remote}${discarded_source}/"; then
            say "  ${remote}${discarded_source}  ->  ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}-replaced"
            [ "${discarded_planned}" = 1 ] || plan="${plan:+${plan},}discarded"
            discarded_planned=1
        fi
    done
    # The content folder derived beside the saves moves too (the same test
    # the items count makes below). It was moved and never listed here, so
    # the hub's preview said less than --apply did (2026-10-01).
    if moving_content "${saves}" "${content}" && has_entries "${remote}${content}/"; then
