        say "  ${remote}${content}  ->  ${remote}${NEW_CONTENT}"; plan="${plan:+${plan},}content"
    fi

    if [ "${mode}" != "--apply" ]; then
        # One line the interface reads (the TIDY UP row's description says
        # what moves and where): the tiers holding files, in move order --
        # backups, saves, discarded, content -- or none when only a setting
        # would change. The row named /ROCKNIX on a build whose folder is
        # /pixelelated until this line existed (2026-10-01).
        echo ">>> plan ${plan:-none} ${NEW_ROOT}"
        say ""
        say "Nothing has been changed. Run with --apply to do it."
        return 0
    fi

    say ""
    migration_record_save begin || return $?
    # What moves, counted before anything does, so the page reads ITEM 1 OF n
    # from the first announcement (D-UI-026); each tier announces itself in
    # the page's own words as its move begins. A tier with nothing stored
    # moves only its pointer and is not an item.
    local items=0 item=0
    ! same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}" && has_entries "${remote}${backups}/" && items=$((items + 1))
    ! same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}" && has_files "${remote}${saves_src}/" && items=$((items + 1))
    ! same_folder "${old_replaced}" "${NEW_SAVES}-replaced" && has_entries "${remote}${old_replaced}/" && items=$((items + 1))
    moving_content "${saves}" "${content}" && has_entries "${remote}${content}/" && items=$((items + 1))
    announce() { item=$((item + 1)); echo ">>> unit $1|${item}|${items}"; }
    # The backups first (PL-025). In the original layout they sit inside the
    # saves folder; moved first, they are out of it before the saves move
    # looks, as well as excluded from it. Each pointer is written as its
    # tier lands (PL-026), only once the data is where it will point: a
    # config updated first, then a move that failed, is a device looking at
    # an empty folder and reporting that it has no saves. A tier with
    # nothing stored only has its pointer moved.
    if ! same_folder "${backups}" "${NEW_BACKUPS}"; then
        if has_entries "${remote}${backups}/"; then
            announce "SETTINGS BACKUPS"
            if ! relocate "${remote}${backups}" "${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}" "backups" SETTINGS_REMOTE; then
                say "Nothing else attempted."
                return 5
            fi
        else
            set_pointer SETTINGS_REMOTE "${NEW_BACKUPS}" || return 5
        fi
    fi

    migration_record_save backups || return $?
    local moved_saves=0
    if ! same_folder "${saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then
        if has_files "${remote}${saves_src}/"; then
            announce "SAVES"
            relocate "${remote}${saves_src}" "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}" "saves" SAVES_REMOTE "${SAVES_EXCLUDES[@]}" || return 5
            moved_saves=1
        else
            set_pointer SAVES_REMOTE "${NEW_SAVES}" || return 5
        fi
        # Only a missing content choice follows automatically. An explicit
        # empty value selects the cloud root and must survive the move (#380).
        if content_unset; then
            set_pointer CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEW_CONTENT}" || return 5
            content="${NEW_CONTENT}"
        fi
    fi
    migration_record_save saves || return $?
    if ! same_folder "${old_replaced}" "${NEW_SAVES}-replaced" && has_entries "${remote}${old_replaced}/"; then
        announce "DISCARDED SAVES"
        if ! relocate "${remote}${old_replaced}" "${remote}${NEW_SAVES}-replaced" "discarded saves" ""; then
            say "Your discarded saves didn't finish moving; they are still at ${remote}${old_replaced}. Try again."
            return 5
        fi
    fi

    migration_record_save discarded || return $?
    # ROMs move with the saves they belong to, when the pointer is one we
    # derived. A CONTENT_REMOTE the owner set themselves is theirs, and stays.
    # Its result is the run's (audit #307 PL-071): a content move that was
    # refused or failed used to be followed by "Done." and exit 0, so the
    # card said the tidy had completed while the ROMs stayed behind.
    local content_rc=0
    # Compared as folders, and never onto itself (PL-001): a saves folder at
    # /ROCKNIX derives /ROCKNIX/Content, the new folder itself, which the
    # string compare sent through the move and so onto itself.
    if moving_content "${saves}" "${content}"; then
        has_entries "${remote}${content}/" && announce "ROMS, BIOS, AND GAME CONTENT"
        migrate_content "${remote}" "${content}" "${mode}" || content_rc=$?
    elif [ -n "${content}" ] && ! same_folder "${content}" "${NEW_CONTENT}"; then
        say "Leaving CONTENT_REMOTE at ${content} -- it is not a path this migration set."
    fi

    say ""
    if [ "${content_rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
        say "Saves are at ${remote}${NEW_SAVES} and backups at ${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}, but your ROMs and BIOS files didn't move. Try again."
        return "${content_rc}"
    fi
    migration_record_save content || return $?
    write_marker "${remote}" || return $?
    # Keep the bound recovery record until every eligible earlier shelf has
    # landed. The primary copy can expose another orphan (or RC2 left both).
    # A saved source survives interruption here without losing the original
    # endpoint/configured-pointer binding. Reuse the verified relocation path.
    if inherited_discarded "${remote}"; then
        if same_folder "${RECOVERY_DISCARDED}" "${old_replaced}" \
           || [ "${recovery_depth}" -ge "${#SUPERSEDED_DEFAULT_SAVES[@]}" ]; then
            say "Your discarded saves didn't finish moving; they are still at ${remote}${RECOVERY_DISCARDED}. Try again."
            echo ">>> why SOME FILES DIDN'T FINISH"
            return 5
        fi
        old_replaced="${RECOVERY_DISCARDED}"
        migration_record_save discarded || return $?
        migration_step_1 "${remote}" "${saves}" "${backups}" "${content}" "${mode}" "$((recovery_depth + 1))"
        return $?
    fi
    migration_record_save complete || return $?
    rm -f "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" || return 5
    sync || return 5
    say "Done. Saves are at ${remote}${NEW_SAVES}, backups at ${remote}${NEW_BACKUPS}."
    [ "${moved_saves}" = "1" ] && say "Old folders were left in place if anything else was in them."
    return 0
}

# --superseded: the list, one per line, for the sync scripts' string test
# before they pay for a network call (no conf, no network, no lock).

# (D-CLOUD-170), asked at every boot, so no network and no rclone start: the

# kept it, and a remote is set up. 0 when it has, 1 when not, 2 when the

if [ "${1:-}" = "--needs-step" ]; then

    if [ -e "${MIGRATION_RECORD}" ]; then

        exit 0

    _keep=$(conf_value LAYOUT_KEEP) || exit 2
    if same_folder "${_saves}" "${NEW_SAVES}"; then

        _content=$(conf_value CONTENT_REMOTE) || exit 2

            grep -q '^\[' /storage/.config/rclone/rclone.conf 2>/dev/null || exit 1

fi

#
# Usage:
#   cloud_content_restore --known-directories  print local/supported directory names
#   cloud_content_restore --list           print top-level remote directories
#   cloud_content_restore <dir> [<dir>..]  copy remote dirs into /storage/roms
#   cloud_content_restore --all            copy the whole remote content root
#   cloud_content_restore --match          preview making this device match;
#                                          writes the plan --apply is held to
#   cloud_content_restore --match --apply  do what the preview planned, no
#                                          more (the only mode that deletes)
#
# The remote content root defaults to the remote's root; set CONTENT_REMOTE in
# /storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf to point somewhere else (e.g. "GAMES").

. /etc/profile

LOG_FILE="/var/log/cloud_sync.log"
SCRIPT_NAME=$(basename "$0")
DEST="/storage/roms"

# Local directory membership shared with cloud_setup discovery. This read-only
# mode needs neither credentials nor a nonempty local library: a fresh device
# still recognizes every system in its installed EmulationStation config.
legacy_dirs() {
    local d base
    for d in "${DEST}"/*/; do
        [ -d "${d}" ] || continue
        base=$(basename "${d}")
        case "${base}" in savefiles|savestates|screenshots|backup) continue ;; esac
        echo "${base}"
    done
}

# Match installed paths, not system labels: several labels differ from the
# actual directory a game uses. The same functions drive --scan below.
es_systems_file() {
    for c in /storage/.config/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg \
             /usr/config/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg; do
        [ -r "${c}" ] && { echo "${c}"; return 0; }
    done
}

supported_systems() {
    local c; c=$(es_systems_file)
    [ -n "${c}" ] || return 0
    sed -n 's:.*<path>/storage/roms/\([^</]*\).*:\1:p' "${c}" | sort -u
}

if [ "${1:-}" = --known-directories ]; then

fi

# The exit that means "nothing ran: another cloud sync holds the lock", which
# EmulationStation names (SKIPPED - ANOTHER CLOUD SYNC IS RUNNING). It was 3
# until 2026-09-09, which is also rclone's "directory not found", so a failed
# unit carrying rclone's code to the final exit read as a sync that was never
# running (#99, blindspot 33). sysexits.h's EX_TEMPFAIL sits above everything
# rclone returns (0-9) and below the 128+signal range, so nothing this script
# forwards can produce it. The same two numbers (75, and 69 for no network --
# raised here when the link goes away under a running unit, see
# stop_no_network) are what EmulationStation reads; scripts and ES ship
# together.
readonly EXIT_LOCK_HELD=75 EXIT_NO_NETWORK=69

log_message() {
    echo "[$(date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")] [INFO] [${SCRIPT_NAME}] ${1}" >> ${LOG_FILE}
}

# One cloud transfer at a time, whoever asked for it.
#
# Three callers can start one: EmulationStation at boot (the startup sync,
# which ran headless from autostart/102-cloud-saves until #94), EmulationStation
# after a game exits, and a person in the menu. Until
# 2026-09-04 the game-exit path was an OS hook with a pgrep guard; moving it
# into ES kept the visible progress and dropped the guard, so exiting a game
# during the boot sync started a second rclone against the same remote. Two
# writers on one folder is how a mirror deleted another handheld's saves
# (D-CLOUD-014); two copies racing is milder, and still nothing anybody asked
# for.
#
# The lock lives here, in the script, so no caller has to know about the
# others. /var/run is tmpfs, so a lock cannot survive a reboot and go stale.
# Non-blocking, because a request that queues silently behind a twenty-minute
# transfer looks exactly like one that hung. Exit EXIT_LOCK_HELD (75) means
# "skipped: another sync is running" -- the UI names it, and no last-run stamp
# is written for work that did not happen.
#
# The descriptor is this shell's and nothing else's. A shell redirection
# carries no close-on-exec, so `exec 9>` hands fd 9 to every child the
# script starts, and rclone then holds the lock for the whole of a transfer
# (watched in /proc on the VM, #124). While the script outlives its
# children that is invisible, because bash waits for each of them before it
# exits. The moment it does not -- killed or orphaned while rclone is still
# copying, a child left in the background -- the lock outlives the run that
# took it and every sync afterwards is refused with "another cloud sync is
# running" when nothing is running at all. So the body runs with fd 9
# closed ("9>&-"): bash keeps the lock on a descriptor of its own, which it
# does mark close-on-exec, and nothing this script starts can see it.
#
# The refusal also waits a moment before saying no, as belt and braces for
# a holder this script does not own: a descriptor leaked by an older build,
# or a process in the act of exiting, frees itself in milliseconds, while a
# real concurrent transfer does not. One second of patience turns a raced
# skip into a run that works and costs a genuinely blocked run one second.
CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK=/var/run/cloud_sync.lock
take_cloud_lock() {
    local tries=0
    exec 9>"${CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK}"
    while ! flock -n 9; do
        if [ "${tries}" -ge 4 ]; then
            echo "Skipped: another cloud sync is already running. Try again when it's done."
            log_message "skipped: another cloud sync holds ${CLOUD_SYNC_LOCK}"
            exit "${EXIT_LOCK_HELD}"
        fi
        tries=$((tries + 1))
        sleep 0.25
    done
}

if [ ! -e "/storage/.config/rclone/rclone.conf" ]; then

# The two values this script needs from cloud_sync.conf, read as text and
# never sourced (audit #307 PL-051's script half): a folder value an earlier
# build wrote with "$(...)" in it ran on every `source`. A CONTENT_REMOTE
# that carries a $, a backtick, a backslash or a control character is not a
# folder name, and the run refuses it rather than use it as a path.
#
# Read in the forms `source` reads (the audit of the fixes, G-A-06/G-A-02):
# the value double quoted, single quoted or bare; after it nothing, or
# blanks and a # comment. The first cut took only KEY=value or KEY="value"
# whole: a trailing comment or single quotes gave an empty CONTENT_REMOTE --
# the cloud's root -- where the folder had been, and the backup went there.
# A line it cannot read as plain text exits 2, and CONTENT_REMOTE's refuses
# the run; nothing is read as the root that did not say the root. Of two
# lines for one key, the first: every saves run EmulationStation starts is
# --yes, which runs cloud_sync_cleanup_duplicates.sh, which keeps the first,
# so that is the value the saves scripts run with and the file is left with.
#
# And a file with a control character but a tab anywhere in it is
# unreadable here as it is to the saves scripts' conf_valid (the audit of
# the fix round, PL-002): this reader never sources the file, but a blank
# is a space or a tab to both, so the tiers run with one reading of one
# file -- a carriage return after a value used to pass here as a blank.
#
# The key set in a form `source` reads and this does not -- indented,
# exported, declared, appended to, or with a blank before the = -- is
# unreadable, never absent (the audit of the fix round, lead G2-A-03):
# read as absent it was the cloud's root, and a content backup went there.
# The saves scripts' conf_valid refuses such a file whole.
conf_get() { # <KEY>: its value, quotes off; nothing when absent; exit 2 when unreadable, and why on stdout
    [ -f /storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf ] || return 0
    awk -v k="$1" '
        { t = $0; gsub(/\t/, "", t); if (t ~ /[[:cntrl:]]/ && !cntrl) cntrl = NR }
        index($0, k "=") != 1 && !other \
            && $0 ~ ("^[ \t]*((export|declare|typeset|readonly|local)([ \t]+-[A-Za-z]+)*[ \t]+)?" k "[ \t]*[+]?=") { other = NR }
        index($0, k "=") == 1 {
            s = substr($0, length(k) + 2); v = ""; r = ""; ok = 1; why = ""
            c = substr(s, 1, 1)
            if (c == "\"") {
                # Inside double quotes bash reads \" \\ \$ and \` as the one
                # character each (PL-015), and so does this; an unescaped $
                # or backtick is an expansion this reader does not make, and
                # any other backslash is refused as conf_valid refuses it.
                n = length(s); i = 2; closed = 0
                while (i <= n) {
                    d = substr(s, i, 1)
                    if (d == "\"") { closed = 1; break }
                    if (d == "\\") {
                        e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
                        if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
                        ok = 0
                        why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
                                        : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
                        break
                    }
                    if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
                    v = v d; i++
                }
                if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
                if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
            } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
                j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
                if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
            } else {
                match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
            }
            if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
            if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }
        }
        END {
            if (cntrl) { print "line " cntrl ": a control character other than a tab"; exit 2 }
            if (other) { print "line " other ": " k " set in a form this reader does not read"; exit 2 }
            if (found && !firstok) { print firstwhy; exit 2 }
            if (found) print first
        }
    ' /storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf
}

# Installed beside this script, also when the host fixtures copy it.

# A probe is a single listing that exists to answer quickly: one attempt,
# tighter than the transfers (the same values the saves scripts probe with).
readonly -a RCLONE_PROBE_OPTS=(--contimeout 10s --timeout 20s --low-level-retries 1 --retries 1)
# A listing's bound (#143): three low-level retries, not a transfer's ten --
# rclone's S3 backend hands the count to the AWS SDK as attempts with
# exponential backoff (see cloud_backup for the measurement).
readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)

# Whole or not at all: to a temporary name beside the stamp, then renamed
# over it, as ThreadedCloudSync::recordOutcome does. A kill mid-write leaves
# the previous stamp; it used to leave an empty file (D-CLOUD-078, #105).
# LAST_WHY, when a `>>> why` line was printed, becomes the stamp's third
# field as a token (spaces to underscores) for the row to read (D-UI-028).
LAST_WHY=""
write_stamp() {
    local file="$1" line="$2" tmp
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${file}")" 2>/dev/null
    tmp="${file}.tmp.$$"
    { printf '%s\n' "${line}" > "${tmp}"; } 2>/dev/null \
        && mv -f "${tmp}" "${file}" 2>/dev/null \
        || rm -f "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null
}
record_outcome() { # <stamp-name> <rc>
    local why=""
    case "$2" in
        0|9|"${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"|"${EXIT_LOCK_HELD}") ;;
        *) [ -n "${LAST_WHY}" ] && why=" $(printf '%s' "${LAST_WHY}" | tr ' ' '_')" ;;
    esac
    write_stamp "/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/last-$1" "$(date +%s) $2${why}"
}

# Why a unit did not finish, in the player's words (D-UI-028, D-CLOUD-077):
# one `>>> why <SENTENCE>` protocol line per failing unit, which the page
# and the card read; rclone's code stays in the log. The sentences are the
# vocabulary table's in es-native-ui.md.
say_why() {
    LAST_WHY="$1"
    echo ">>> why $1"
    log_message "why: $1"
}
why_for() {
    case "$1" in
        3|4) echo "COULDN'T FIND YOUR CLOUD FOLDER" ;;
        5|124) echo "YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING" ;;
        6)   echo "SOME FILES DIDN'T FINISH" ;;
        7|8) echo "YOUR CLOUD WOULDN'T TAKE THE FILES" ;;
        130) echo "IT WAS STOPPED" ;;
        *)   echo "SOMETHING WENT WRONG" ;;
    esac
}

has_default_route() {
    ip -4 route show default 2>/dev/null | grep -q . \
        || ip -6 route show default 2>/dev/null | grep -q .
}

# Is the network gone? Asked after rclone failed, so the run can say why it
# ended rather than hand up a code that reads as FAILED and sends somebody
# to a log. Gone: no default route, or a route through which neither the
# remote nor anything else answers a bounded probe. Not gone: the remote
# answers again (a blip rclone did not survive), or the internet answers
# while the remote does not (the provider, or the sign-in) -- that is
# rclone's failure to report, and the caller passes rclone's code through
# as before. The same three questions cloud_backup asks (#101, #103).
network_gone() {
    has_default_route || return 0
    rclone lsd "${REMOTENAME}" "${RCLONE_PROBE_OPTS[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
    ping -q -c1 -W 3 1.1.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
    ping -q -c1 -W 3 8.8.8.8 >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 1
    return 0
}

# The network went away under a running unit. Says so, records that the run
# did not complete -- never a 0, which would read as a restore that happened
# -- under the stamp the action keeps (last-content-restore, or
# last-content-match for --match --apply), and exits EXIT_NO_NETWORK, which
# EmulationStation names (SKIPPED - NO NETWORK CONNECTION on the card,
# SKIPPED, NO NETWORK on the row). No further unit is attempted: each would
# stall for another minute against the same dead link. rclone copy and sync
# write each file under a temporary name and rename it when complete, so
# nothing partial is left on the card; a match's deletions had already
# happened when the sync ran, and they are final -- a match removes only
# what the cloud does not have (D-CLOUD-023; #308 gpt F-CS-26: this said
# the cloud still held them).
#
# SKIPPED means nothing was touched (#308 claude F-CS-24): when something had
# already moved -- a unit completed, a match removed files -- before the
# network went, the stamp still carries 69 and adds the gaps token and a why,
# "<epoch> 69 gaps YOU WENT OFFLINE PART-WAY THROUGH", which the rows read as
# COULDN'T FINISH (CloudText::parseLastRun takes the token before the code).
# The exit stays 69; the page reads a 69 after progress the same way.
# Did this run's rclone move a file since <offset> into the log? Progress,
# for the stamp stop_no_network writes, is what rclone logged moving --
# "<path>: Copied (...)", "Moved (...)", "Deleted" -- not a unit that
# completed (the audit of the fixes, G-A-08/G-A-13): files a unit moved
# before its own failure did not count, and a unit that moved nothing did.
# Every transfer here logs at INFO to LOG_FILE, and the transfer lock
# keeps any other cloud script from writing it meanwhile.
log_offset() { stat -c %s "${LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }
moved_since() { # <byte offset into LOG_FILE>
    local now
    now=$(stat -c %s "${LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
    [ "${now}" -gt "$1" ] 2>/dev/null || return 1
    tail -c +$(( $1 + 1 )) "${LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null | grep -qE ': (Copied|Moved) \(|: Deleted$'
}
PROGRESS_MADE=0
stop_no_network() {
    local stamp="$1" rc="$2" doing="$3"
    echo "Couldn't finish: lost the network while ${doing}. Try again when you're online."
    log_message "stopped: the network went away while ${doing} (rclone exit ${rc}); exit ${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"
    if [ "${PROGRESS_MADE}" = 1 ]; then
        write_stamp "/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/last-content-${stamp}" "$(date +%s) ${EXIT_NO_NETWORK} gaps YOU WENT OFFLINE PART-WAY THROUGH"
    else
        record_outcome "content-${stamp}" "${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"
    fi
    exit "${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"
}

# Read the old shape, write the new one.
#
# CONTENT_REMOTE is newer than content sync itself. Before it existed, content
# sat at the remote root, and an upgraded device would look in the new place,
# find nothing, and simply show an empty list - the player never chose a
# layout, so there is nothing for them to reason about, and nobody reads
# release notes on a handheld.
#
# So restore looks in the configured location and falls back to the old one.
# Backups always write to the configured location, so a library migrates by
# itself the next time it is backed up, with no prompt and no migration step.
# The legacy root on a path-based remote is the whole account, which holds the
# owner's own folders too. Only directories this device actually has locally
# are offered from there - listing somebody's holiday photos as restorable ROMs
# would be worse than the empty list this fixes.

# Where a local directory lives in the current cloud layout.
#
# ROMs and BIOS are named folders rather than a mirror of /storage/roms,
# because the person filling them in is looking at a file manager on a
# computer, where "bios sitting beside snes" is an accident of how a handheld
# stores things. The local name is what everything else here uses, so the
# mapping stays in one place: bios lives under BIOS, everything else under
# ROMs.
remote_for() {
    case "$1" in
        bios) echo "${ROOT}BIOS" ;;
        *)    echo "${ROOT}ROMs/$1" ;;
    esac
}

# Returns the full remote path that actually holds this directory.
#
# Three shapes are in the field and all of them have to keep working:
#
#   1. ROMs/<system> and BIOS      -- current
#   2. <system> and bios, flat under CONTENT_REMOTE  -- what shipped before this
#   3. <system> at the remote root -- before CONTENT_REMOTE existed at all
#
# Read all three, write only the first (cloud_content_backup). A library then
# migrates itself the next time it is backed up: nothing to prompt about,
# nothing to explain, and a device that has not updated yet still finds its
# content where it left it.
#
# The legacy root on a path-based remote is the whole account, which holds the
# owner's own folders too. Only directories this device actually has locally
# are offered from there - listing somebody's holiday photos as restorable ROMs
# would be worse than the empty list this fixes.
resolve_src() {
    local dir="$1" new
    new="$(remote_for "${dir}")"
    if exists_remote "${new}"; then
        echo "${new}"
    elif rclone lsf --dirs-only "${ROOT}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sed 's:/$::' | grep -qx "${dir}"; then
        log_message "Content \"${dir}\" found in the flat pre-ROMs layout"
        echo "${ROOT}${dir}"
    elif [ -n "${CONTENT_REMOTE}" ] && legacy_dirs | grep -qx "${dir}" \
         && rclone lsf --dirs-only "${LEGACY_ROOT}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sed 's:/$::' | grep -qx "${dir}"; then
        log_message "Content \"${dir}\" found at the pre-CONTENT_REMOTE location"
        echo "${LEGACY_ROOT}${dir}"
    else
        echo "${new}"
    fi
}

# Does a remote path exist?
#
# NOT `rclone lsjson --stat`, which is what this used to be. On bucket-based
# remotes (S3, B2, Minio) stat synthesises a directory entry for *any* path --
# verified against Minio on rclone 1.60 and 1.74, where
# "utterly-bogus-never-created" reports success with IsDir true. So it can
# never report absence there, and every caller that branched on it took the
# "exists" path unconditionally.
#
# A listing can report absence. Two questions, because a directory can be real
# without holding files: does it contain anything, or does its parent list it
# (which is what an --s3-directory-markers marker object produces)?
exists_remote() {
    [ -n "$(rclone lsf "$1" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ] && return 0
    local parent name
    parent="${1%/}"; name="${parent##*/}"; parent="${parent%/*}"
    [ -n "${name}" ] || return 1
    rclone lsf --dirs-only "${parent}/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | grep -qx "${name}/"
}

# Is this remote path missing, rather than unreadable? rclone answers "not
# found" (exit 3) when the server's reply is the one it maps to that, and a
# plain error (exit 1) when the words differ: an FTP server that answers a
# missing folder with 501 "No such directory." where the standard reply is
# 550 makes every "is it there yet?" branch read as "the cloud is broken"
# (#142, from the #133 matrix). The parent settles it, whatever the words:
# walk up until a level lists. A level that lists and lacks the next name is
# a path not created yet (0); one that lists and holds it means the failure
# was something else (1); a remote whose root will not list is broken (1).
# On a bucket an absent prefix lists as empty, which is the same answer
# (D-CLOUD-120). Called only after a listing has already failed with a code
# other than 3, so the everyday path costs nothing extra.
absent_not_broken() {
    local path="${1%/}" remote rel name parent listing
    remote="${path%%:*}:"; rel="${path#*:}"; rel="${rel#/}"
    while [ -n "${rel}" ]; do
        name="${rel##*/}"; parent="${rel%/*}"
        [ "${parent}" = "${rel}" ] && parent=""
        if listing=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "${remote}/${parent:+${parent}/}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
            printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- "${name}/" && return 1
            return 0
        fi
        [ -n "${parent}" ] || return 1
        rel="${parent}"
    done
    return 1
}

# Which systems this device syncs.
#
# One cloud library, many handhelds, and they are not interchangeable: an H700
# cannot run GameCube, and a 3:2 panel makes a device a Game Boy Advance
# machine by preference rather than by limit. So the set is a per-device
# choice.
#
# Kept in /storage/.cache, deliberately. The obvious homes -- cloud_sync.conf,
# or ES's system.cfg -- are both captured by the settings backup, and restoring
# one device's selection onto another would silently change what that device
# syncs. That is the same defect shape as the CONTENT_REMOTE split (6717e0b348),
# and once was enough.
#
# No file means no selection means everything, so a device that has never
# opened the picker behaves exactly as it did before.
SELECTION="/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/content-systems"

# Only a system folder's name is ever acted on (audit #307 PL-030):
# --set-systems refuses any other since that change, and a selection an
# earlier build wrote without the check is read past a line that is not
# one, never with it.
selected_systems() {
    [ -r "${SELECTION}" ] || return 0
    grep -E '^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$' "${SELECTION}" 2>/dev/null
}

# Total bytes per top-level directory, from ONE recursive listing.
#
# rclone size per system would be one API round trip each, which on a library
# of thirty systems is thirty waits before the player sees anything. lsf
# --format sp returns size and path for every file in a single call; summing
# them here costs nothing.
sizes_under() {
    rclone lsf -R --files-only --format "sp" --separator "|" "$1" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null \
        | grep -v '|README\.txt$' \
        | awk -F'|' '{ i = index($2, "/"); if (i == 0) next;
                       d = substr($2, 1, i - 1); sz[d] += $1 }
                     END { for (d in sz) print d "|" sz[d] }'
}


# --- make this device match the cloud ------------------------------------
#
# Backup and restore are both copy-only, deliberately, so a system removed
# from the cloud stays on the device forever and a card can never be made to
# match the library. This is the third action, and the only one here that
# deletes.
#
# Five rules, each of which has already cost something in this subsystem:
#
#  1. --delete-excluded NEVER appears. Save files live inside system
#     directories; with the excludes in place rclone leaves excluded
#     destination files alone, and that one flag inverts it into a save wipe.
#  2. Only ROMs/<selected system> and BIOS. /storage/roms also holds
#     savefiles, savestates, screenshots, backup, bezels, themes and music --
#     other tiers' or nobody's.
#  3. An empty or failed listing must never mean "delete everything". A wifi
#     drop, a lapsed token and a renamed cloud folder all look exactly like an
#     empty cloud, so the content root is positively confirmed to hold
#     something before any deletion is considered.
#  4. Cloud -> device only. The mirror direction is what deleted another
#     handheld's whole save library on 2026-09-01 (D-CLOUD-014).
#  5. Saves survive a removed system. Its content goes; the .srm and .state
#     files stay, leaving the directory holding only those -- which
#     has_content() correctly reports as no content.
#
# Deletions are final on the device: no local backup-dir. The space reclaimed
# is the entire point of syncing ROMs selectively, and the cloud is the backup
# by definition, since this only ever removes what the cloud does not have
# (D-CLOUD-023). Preview first, then apply.

# Defined here, above every consumer.
#
# They used to sit below the case statement, which was fine while the only
# consumer was the transfer loop at the end of the file -- and silently
# catastrophic the moment --match started calling them from inside the case.
# Bash expands an unset array to nothing, so rclone ran with no save
# excludes at all and a match would have deleted .srm and .state files. It
# was invisible in the output: fewer exclusions simply means more deletions,
# and the preview reported them as ordinary work.

# What the saves tier owns, and content must never carry.
#
# A system directory holds more than games: RetroArch writes .srm and .state
# next to the ROM, and several systems keep memory cards in a subfolder. The
# saves allowlist claims all of it ("+ /**/*.srm" and friends in
# cloud_sync-rules.txt), so uploading a system folder wholesale puts saves
# in a second cloud location under different rules -- two writers and no
# reconciliation, which is exactly how 70 files were deleted on 2026-09-01.
#
# Worse in the other direction: a content restore would then copy stale saves
# back over live ones.
#
# The earlier allowlist fix (d77d4ea44d) covered directories another tier
# owns. This is the same rule one level down, for files. Kept in step with
# cloud_sync-rules.txt by hand -- there is no shared parser, and a pattern
# added there must be added here. .fla was added there (#89, N64's flash
# saves beside the ROM) and not here, so a content backup uploaded it and
# a match removed it as content (the audit's gpt F-CS-02).
SAVE_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "*.srm" --exclude "*.sav" --exclude "*.fs"
    --exclude "*.state*" --exclude "*.auto" --exclude "*.dsv*"
    --exclude "*.eep" --exclude "*.mpk" --exclude "*.sra" --exclude "*.fla"
    --exclude "*.mcd" --exclude "*.mcr"
    --exclude "save/**" --exclude "memcards/**"
    --exclude "shared/savefiles/**" --exclude "PPSSPP/**"
)

# Another sync client's unresolved dispute is not our content.
#
# Dropbox and Nextcloud rename the losing side of a concurrent write to
# "X (Someone's conflicted copy 2026-09-03)"; Syncthing appends
# ".sync-conflict-<date>". Carrying those onto a handheld doubles the storage
# for no benefit -- the player cannot resolve a conflict from a games menu --
# and it makes the artifacts immortal: a device that downloaded them uploads
# them again on the next backup, so deleting them in the cloud looks like the
# provider putting them back. That happened here, to 271 directories of BIOS
# (2026-09-04).
#
# Resolution belongs on the computer where both sides can be seen. We decline
# to move them in either direction, which is also the only way a cleanup on
# one side stays done.
CONFLICT_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "**conflicted copy**"
    --exclude "**.sync-conflict-**"
    --exclude "*.????????.partial"
)

# gamelist.xml travels on its own terms.
#
# It is the scraping payload -- names, descriptions, genres, ratings, media
# paths and the cheevos hashes that cost a hash of every ROM -- and all of that
# is device-independent, so sharing it means scraping once rather than once per
# handheld. Paths inside it are relative ("./Mega Man 3 (USA).zip"), so it
# carries across devices unchanged.
#
# It degrades well in both directions, which is why this is safe at all:
#
#   * Reading, EmulationStation builds its list from the filesystem first and
#     skips any entry whose ROM is absent ("does not exist ... Ignoring"), so a
#     52-entry list on a handheld holding 10 of those games shows 10 games and
#     no phantoms. That holds while ParseGamelistOnly is false, which is the
#     default.
#   * Writing, updateGamelist re-reads the file and rewrites only the entries
#     whose metadata changed, preserving entries for ROMs this device does not
#     have -- deliberately, per its own comment.
#
# What neither of those protects against is rclone, which replaces a file
# wholesale. A device that scans its own ROMs and uploads before it has ever
# restored would push a thin list over a rich one. That is an ordering problem,
# not a merge problem, and --update solves it: skip when the destination is
# newer, so the freshest list wins rather than the last writer.
#
# Hence a separate pass. --update on the whole content transfer would also
# apply to ROMs, where "destination is newer" is not a reason to skip a file
# somebody deliberately re-uploaded.
#
# Three fields remain genuinely per-device -- playcount, lastplayed and
# gametime, which EmulationStation itself marks isStatistic and refuses to let
# a scrape overwrite. A file-level sync cannot make that distinction, so those
# are last-writer-wins across devices. Everything else in the file is authored
# or scraped, and favorite is explicitly not a statistic in ES's model.
GAMELIST_ONLY=( --include "gamelist.xml" --include "**/gamelist.xml" )

# What EmulationStation owns, which a content match must never delete.
#
# gamelist.xml carries <playcount>, <lastplayed> and <favorite> -- per-device
# facts that exist nowhere else -- and images/, videos/ and manuals/ hold
# scraped artwork that can represent hours of scraping. None of it is content
# the cloud is authoritative about, so "the cloud does not have it" is not a
# reason to remove it.
#
# Found the only way these things are ever found: reading a real dry run,
# which listed "gamelist.xml: Skipped delete" for every system on the device.
#
# Deliberately scoped to the match path. Whether backup should *upload* a
# gamelist is a separate and open question (#61) -- but deleting one locally
# is wrong under every answer to it.
METADATA_EXCLUDES=(
    --exclude "gamelist.xml"
    --exclude "**/gamelist.xml"
    --exclude "images/**"
    --exclude "videos/**"
    --exclude "manuals/**"
    --exclude "magazines/**"
    --exclude "media/**"
)

# rclone reports sizes in a NOTICE line using human units ("6.090Ki", "64Ki")
# when the destination is local, and bare bytes for a small local-to-local
# copy. Parsing only digits silently produced zero for every real transfer.
to_bytes() {
    awk '{ n = $0 + 0; u = $0; gsub(/[0-9.]/, "", u)
           if (u == "Ki") n *= 1024
           else if (u == "Mi") n *= 1048576
           else if (u == "Gi") n *= 1073741824
           else if (u == "Ti") n *= 1099511627776
           printf "%d\n", n }'
}

# Does the content root actually hold anything? Rule 3.
cloud_root_populated() {
    local n
    n=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "${ROOT}ROMs/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | grep -c . )
    [ "${n}" -gt 0 ] && return 0
    rclone lsf --files-only "${ROOT}BIOS/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q . && return 0
    return 1
}

# What one system would gain and lose. Prints "<sys>|<verb>|<files>|<bytes>",
# or "<sys>|fail|<rclone exit>|0" when it cannot be told.
#
# The counting uses rclone against the local path with the very same exclude
# arrays the transfer uses, rather than a second hand-written find predicate:
# a deletion predicate that can drift from the transfer predicate is how saves
# get deleted by a tool that believes it is only touching ROMs.
#
# Absent is something the cloud says, never something a failure implies
# (rule 3, audit #307 PL-001). The system's listing is read apart from its
# emptiness: exit 0 with nothing listed, or rclone's 3/4 ("not found"), is a
# system the cloud does not have. Any other exit -- a 429 after rclone's own
# retries, the link dropping between two calls -- is asked of the parent
# (absent_not_broken, #142's walk, for a server whose "missing" rclone does
# not map to 3); a parent that lists the system, or will not list at all,
# makes the answer "could not tell", and a system that cannot be told is
# neither planned nor touched. The listing used to be `lsf | grep -q .`,
# which read a failed call as an empty folder and planned `remove`; apply
# then deleted the whole system on a transient error. The dry run and the
# local count are read the same way: a count that failed is not a zero.
match_plan_one() {
    local sys="$1" src local_dir n b out listing lrc
    src="$(remote_for "${sys}")"
    local_dir="${DEST}/${sys}"

    [ -d "${local_dir}" ] || { printf '%s|none|0|0\n' "${sys}"; return 0; }

    listing=$(rclone lsf "${src}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); lrc=$?
    case "${lrc}" in
        0|3|4) ;;
        *)
            if absent_not_broken "${src}"; then
                log_message "match: ${sys} listing failed (rclone exit ${lrc}); its parent lists and lacks it, so it is absent"
                lrc=3
            else
                log_message "match: ${sys} could not be listed (rclone exit ${lrc}); not planned"
                printf '%s|fail|%s|0\n' "${sys}" "${lrc}"
                return 0
            fi ;;
    esac

    if [ "${lrc}" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "${listing}" ]; then
        # Present in the cloud: sync reconciles both directions of difference.
        out=$(bounded_content_rclone sync "${src}" "${local_dir}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" \
                "${SAVE_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${CONFLICT_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${METADATA_EXCLUDES[@]}" \
                --dry-run --stats 0 2>&1)
        lrc=$?
        if [ "${lrc}" -ne 0 ]; then
            log_message "match: ${sys} dry run failed (rclone exit ${lrc}); not planned"
            printf '%s|fail|%s|0\n' "${sys}" "${lrc}"
            return 0
        fi
        # "NOTICE: Game3.zip: Skipped delete as --dry-run is set (size 5)" --
        # the exact wording on rclone 1.75.0, read off the real output rather
        # than taken from the documentation. The size in the tail is what lets
        # the confirmation say how much space comes back.
        n=$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | grep -c "Skipped delete")
        b=$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | sed -n 's/.*Skipped delete.*(size \([0-9.KMGTi]*\)).*/\1/p' \
              | to_bytes | awk '{ t += $1 } END { print t+0 }')
        printf '%s|sync|%s|%s\n' "${sys}" "${n}" "${b}"
    else
        # Absent from the cloud entirely: its content goes, its saves stay.
        out=$(rclone size "${local_dir}" \
                "${SAVE_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${CONFLICT_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${METADATA_EXCLUDES[@]}" 2>/dev/null)
        lrc=$?
        n=$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | sed -n 's/^Total objects: *\([0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1)
        b=$(printf '%s\n' "${out}" | sed -n 's/^Total size: .*(\([0-9]*\) Byte).*/\1/p' | head -1)
        if [ "${lrc}" -ne 0 ] || [ -z "${n}" ]; then
            log_message "match: ${sys} could not be counted on this device (rclone exit ${lrc}); not planned"
            printf '%s|fail|%s|0\n' "${sys}" "${lrc}"
            return 0
        fi
        [ -n "${b}" ] || b=0
        [ "${n}" -eq 0 ] && { printf '%s|none|0|0\n' "${sys}"; return 0; }
        printf '%s|remove|%s|%s\n' "${sys}" "${n}" "${b}"
    fi
}

# The saves restore's record that the tree under it holds no leftover of a
# cut transfer (cloud_restore's PARTIALS_CLEAN, #308 claude F-CS-08): this
# script writes into the same tree, so it takes the record down while it
# writes and puts it back only when it ended by itself with nothing of its
# own left over -- a failed unit's folder is swept for rclone's
# <name>.<8>.partial before that. A run of this cut part-way leaves the
# record down, and the next saves restore walks the tree (the audit of the
# fixes, claude G-A-07: the record said clean across a content restore
# that was cut, and the next content backup sent the leftover as a ROM).
TREE_CLEAN=/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/restore-tree-clean
TREE_CLEAN_AT_START=0
tree_record_take() { [ -e "${TREE_CLEAN}" ] && TREE_CLEAN_AT_START=1; rm -f "${TREE_CLEAN}" 2>/dev/null; }
tree_record_give() { [ "${TREE_CLEAN_AT_START}" = 1 ] && : > "${TREE_CLEAN}" 2>/dev/null; return 0; }
sweep_partials() { [ -d "$1" ] || return 0; find "$1" -type f -name '*.????????.partial' -exec rm -f {} + 2>/dev/null; }

# The plan the player agreed to (audit #307 PL-001, F-CS-03). The preview
# writes one line per system it checked -- "<sys>|<verb>|<files>|<bytes>",
# none included -- under a header naming the moment, whole or not at all,
# and only when every system could be told; apply reads it and holds each
# system to it: the same verb, no more to remove than the preview counted,
# and that count, not its own, is --max-delete. A system the plan does not
# name, or whose verb changed since, is refused rather than recomputed and
# run. The plan is spent by the apply that reads it, so each apply stands on
# the preview that immediately led to it. Device-local, under /storage/.cache
# like the stamps: a plan restored onto another device would describe
# another card.
MATCH_PLAN="/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/content-match-plan"
match_plan_write() { # <plan lines>
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${MATCH_PLAN}")" 2>/dev/null
    { printf 'plan %s\n' "$(date +%s)"; printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep '|'; } > "${MATCH_PLAN}.tmp.$$" 2>/dev/null \
        && mv -f "${MATCH_PLAN}.tmp.$$" "${MATCH_PLAN}" 2>/dev/null \
        || { rm -f "${MATCH_PLAN}.tmp.$$" 2>/dev/null; return 1; }
}
match_plan_of() { # <sys>: its line from the plan, or nothing
    [ -n "${MATCH_PLAN_TEXT}" ] || return 1
    printf '%s\n' "${MATCH_PLAN_TEXT}" | awk -F'|' -v s="$1" '$1 == s { print; exit }'
}

# What a match removed, as rclone reports it (#308 gpt F-CS-26). Before a
# system runs, its content files are listed with their sizes by the same
# excludes the run uses; its rclone writes a log of its own, whose
# "<path>: Deleted" lines name what went; the count and the bytes are
# those names looked up in the list, added to the run's totals. The log is
# then appended to the script's own.
MATCH_LOG=""
MATCH_BEFORE=""
match_before() { # <sys>
    MATCH_LOG=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud-match-log.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null) || MATCH_LOG="/tmp/cloud-match-log.$$"
    MATCH_BEFORE=$(mktemp /tmp/cloud-match-before.XXXXXX 2>/dev/null) || MATCH_BEFORE="/tmp/cloud-match-before.$$"
    : > "${MATCH_LOG}"
    rclone lsf -R --files-only --format "sp" --separator "|" "${DEST}/$1" \
        "${SAVE_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${CONFLICT_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${METADATA_EXCLUDES[@]}" > "${MATCH_BEFORE}" 2>/dev/null
}
match_count() { # <sys>: adds what the log says went to the totals
    local counted cfiles cbytes
    counted=$(awk -F'|' -v L="${MATCH_BEFORE}" '
        BEGIN { while ((getline x < L) > 0) { i = index(x, "|"); sz[substr(x, i + 1)] = substr(x, 1, i - 1) } }
        / : .*: Deleted$/ { p = $0; sub(/^.* : /, "", p); sub(/: Deleted$/, "", p); n++; b += sz[p] }
        END { print n + 0 "|" b + 0 }' "${MATCH_LOG}" 2>/dev/null)
    IFS='|' read -r cfiles cbytes <<< "${counted:-0|0}"
    [ "${cfiles}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null && PROGRESS_MADE=1
    # A sync's copies down are progress too (G-A-08).
    grep -qE ': (Copied|Moved) \(' "${MATCH_LOG}" 2>/dev/null && PROGRESS_MADE=1
    total_removed=$((total_removed + cfiles))
    total_bytes=$((total_bytes + cbytes))
    removed_detail="${removed_detail}${removed_detail:+,}$1:${cfiles}:${cbytes}"
    cat "${MATCH_LOG}" >> "${LOG_FILE}" 2>/dev/null
    rm -f "${MATCH_LOG}" "${MATCH_BEFORE}"
}

match_run() {
    local apply="$1" sys line verb files bytes rc=0 sync_rc=0 del_rc=0 total_removed=0

    # The exclusions are the only thing standing between this and somebody's
    # saves, so assert they exist rather than trusting the file's layout. An
    # unset array expands to nothing and rclone would happily proceed.
    if [ ${#SAVE_EXCLUDES[@]} -eq 0 ] || [ ${#METADATA_EXCLUDES[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "Refusing: the rules that keep your saves safe aren't loaded."
        log_message "match: refused, exclusion arrays empty"
        return 1
    fi

    # The preview is read-only and may run beside a transfer; applying is one.
    [ "${apply}" = "1" ] && take_cloud_lock
    # As at the foot of the script: the rest of the run cannot leak the
    # lock into rclone. Closing a descriptor that was never opened (the
    # preview, which takes no lock) is a no-op.
    {

    if ! cloud_root_populated; then
        echo "Refusing to change anything: your cloud's ROMs and BIOS folder looks empty."
        echo "That looks the same whether it really is empty, you're offline, or the"
        echo "folder was renamed - so nothing is removed."
        log_message "match: refused, content root lists nothing"
        # One of the three it can tell apart: with the network gone the
        # refusal is the no-network skip, and says so with the code
        # EmulationStation names. Nothing ran, so no stamp.
        if network_gone; then
            echo "Skipped: there's no network connection. Try again when you're online."
            log_message "match: skipped, no network"
            exit "${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"
        fi
        return 1
    fi

    mapfile -t SYS < <(selected_systems)
    if [ ${#SYS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        echo "You haven't picked any systems for this device yet."
        return 1
    fi

    # The plan (PL-001): a preview starts from none and writes its own at the
    # end; an apply reads the one the preview left and spends it before
    # anything runs, so a second apply cannot stand on the same agreement.
    MATCH_PLAN_TEXT=""
    local plan_lines="" pverb pfiles pbytes
    if [ "${apply}" = "1" ]; then
        if [ -s "${MATCH_PLAN}" ] && head -1 "${MATCH_PLAN}" | grep -q '^plan [0-9][0-9]*$'; then
            MATCH_PLAN_TEXT=$(tail -n +2 "${MATCH_PLAN}")
        fi
        rm -f "${MATCH_PLAN}" 2>/dev/null
        # Spent means gone (the audit of the fix round, lead G2-A-04): a
        # plan the cache would not let go stayed for the next apply, which
        # then stood on a preview it did not follow. One that cannot be
        # removed is not used.
        if [ -e "${MATCH_PLAN}" ]; then
            echo "Nothing was removed: something went wrong on this device. Try again."
            log_message "match: refused, the preview plan ${MATCH_PLAN} could not be removed, so it could not be spent"
            say_why "SOMETHING WENT WRONG"
            record_outcome content-match 1
            return 1
        fi
        if [ -z "${MATCH_PLAN_TEXT}" ]; then
            # No check behind this apply at all -- run on its own, or run
            # again after the apply that spent the plan -- is not a change
            # since a check; the why names what is missing (vm-qa run 68:
            # the round-trip ran --apply alone and was told SOMETHING
            # CHANGED SINCE YOU CHECKED).
            echo "Nothing was removed: check what would change first, then try again."
            log_message "match: refused, no preview plan to apply"
            say_why "CHECK WHAT WOULD CHANGE FIRST"
            record_outcome content-match 1
            return 1
        fi
        # It writes into the saves restore's tree (G-A-07).
        tree_record_take
    else
        rm -f "${MATCH_PLAN}" 2>/dev/null
    fi

    # What the page that runs this shows when it is done. A match is mostly
    # deletion, and rclone's own totals for a deletion read "0 B / 0 B" --
    # true and useless (maintainer, 2026-09-07). So each system is announced
    # as a unit while it runs, and the summary at the end names what went:
    # the numbers the confirmation showed, per system, so the last screen
    # answers the first one.
    local total_bytes=0 removed_detail="" unit_i=0 unit_n=${#SYS[@]} planned
    for sys in "${SYS[@]}"; do
        unit_i=$((unit_i + 1))
        # Every chosen system is an item on the page, announced before its
        # own dry run -- so the page names what is being checked while the
        # check runs -- and announced whether or not it turns out to need
        # anything. The page shows ITEM i OF n with this script's n, so n has
        # to be the number of announcements the run makes and i their running
        # count; until 2026-09-09 a system with nothing to do was skipped
        # without one, and a run over three systems ended on ITEM 2 OF 3
        # (#95). "Already matches the cloud" is that item's outcome, not a
        # reason to hide it, and counting the work first would have held the
        # page on WORKING with no item through one dry run per system. The
        # preview (apply=0) prints plan lines for the confirmation and no
        # markers, as before.
        [ "${apply}" = "1" ] && echo ">>> unit ${sys}|${unit_i}|${unit_n}"
        planned=$(match_plan_one "${sys}")
        IFS='|' read -r _ verb files bytes <<< "${planned}"
        if [ "${apply}" = "1" ] && [ "${verb}" != "fail" ] && [ "${verb}" != "none" ]; then
            # Held to the preview: the same verb, and no more to remove than
            # it counted -- a ROM added since, or a system gone from the
            # cloud since, is not what the player agreed to. The preview's
            # count, not this one, is what --max-delete is given.
            pverb=""; pfiles=""; pbytes=""
            IFS='|' read -r _ pverb pfiles pbytes <<< "$(match_plan_of "${sys}")"
            if [ -z "${pverb}" ] || [ "${verb}" != "${pverb}" ] \
               || ! [ "${files}" -le "${pfiles:-0}" ] 2>/dev/null; then
                echo "Nothing was removed from ${sys}: it changed since you checked. Check again to see what would change."
                log_message "match: ${sys} refused: previewed ${pverb:-nothing}|${pfiles:--}, now ${verb}|${files}"
                say_why "SOMETHING CHANGED SINCE YOU CHECKED"
                rc=1
                continue
            fi
            files="${pfiles}"; bytes="${pbytes}"
        fi
        [ "${apply}" = "1" ] || plan_lines="${plan_lines}${planned}"$'\n'
        case "${verb}" in
            fail)
                # A system that could not be told is neither planned nor
                # touched (PL-001). With the network gone the run is the
                # no-network skip, as everywhere else here; otherwise the
                # preview says so and plans nothing, and an apply says why.
                if [ "${apply}" = "1" ]; then
                    echo "Couldn't check ${sys} against your cloud, so nothing was removed from it."
                else
                    echo "Couldn't check ${sys} against your cloud. Try again."
                fi
                if network_gone; then
                    if [ "${apply}" = "1" ]; then
                        echo ">>> removed ${total_removed}|${total_bytes}|${removed_detail}"
                        stop_no_network match "${files}" "checking ${sys} against the cloud"
                    fi
                    echo "Skipped: there's no network connection. Try again when you're online."
                    exit "${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"
                fi
                [ "${apply}" = "1" ] && say_why "$(why_for "${files}")"
                rc=${files}
                [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ] 2>/dev/null || rc=1
                continue
            ;;
            none)
                [ "${apply}" = "1" ] && echo "Nothing to remove from ${sys}: it already matches the cloud."
                continue
            ;;
            remove)
                if [ "${apply}" = "1" ]; then
                    echo "Removing ${files} files from ${sys} that aren't in your cloud..."
                    match_before "${sys}"
                    rclone delete "${DEST}/${sys}" \
                        "${SAVE_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${CONFLICT_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${METADATA_EXCLUDES[@]}" \
                        --max-delete "${files}" \
                        --log-file "${MATCH_LOG}" --log-level INFO
                    del_rc=$?
                    match_count "${sys}"
                    if [ ${del_rc} -ne 0 ]; then
                        rc=${del_rc}
                        log_message "match: removing ${sys}: rclone exit ${del_rc}"
                        echo "Couldn't finish removing files from ${sys}: $(why_for "${del_rc}" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')."
                        say_why "$(why_for "${del_rc}")"
                    fi
                    rmdir "${DEST}/${sys}" 2>/dev/null
                else
                    echo "${sys}|remove|${files}|${bytes}"
                fi
            ;;
            sync)
                if [ "${apply}" = "1" ]; then
                    echo "Matching ${sys} to the cloud..."
                    # --max-delete is the fail-closed half: if reality has
                    # drifted from the preview the player agreed to, this
                    # aborts rather than deleting more than they saw.
                    #
                    # It is a cap, not a transaction. Measured on rclone
                    # 1.75.0: given three deletions and --max-delete 2, it
                    # exits 7 having already removed two. So it bounds the
                    # damage to what was previewed and does not undo it --
                    # the removals are final (D-CLOUD-023), which is why a
                    # count above the preview's is refused before this runs.
                    match_before "${sys}"
                    bounded_content_rclone sync "$(remote_for "${sys}")" "${DEST}/${sys}" "${RCLONE_NET_OPTS_ARRAY[@]}" \
                        "${SAVE_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${CONFLICT_EXCLUDES[@]}" "${METADATA_EXCLUDES[@]}" \
                        --max-delete "${files}" \
                        --progress --stats 1s \
                        --log-file "${MATCH_LOG}" --log-level INFO
                    sync_rc=$?
                    match_count "${sys}"
                    if [ ${sync_rc} -ne 0 ]; then
                        rc=${sync_rc}
                        sweep_partials "${DEST}/${sys}"
                        # A failed unit says why: the network gone ends the
                        # run as 69 here, anything else carries rclone's own
                        # code up as before. Before the 69 exit, the running
                        # totals go out on the same `>>> removed` line the
                        # completed run prints, so the page can report the
                        # deletions that did happen -- a match is mostly
                        # deletion, and it had already run for every system
                        # before this one (D-UI-028; #105). The totals are
                        # what rclone reports removed (match_count), within
                        # what the player agreed to; what was removed is what
                        # the cloud does not have, so it is gone (D-CLOUD-023).
                        if network_gone; then
                            echo ">>> removed ${total_removed}|${total_bytes}|${removed_detail}"
                            stop_no_network match "${sync_rc}" "matching ${sys} to the cloud"
                        fi
                        log_message "match: matching ${sys}: rclone exit ${sync_rc}"
                        echo "Couldn't finish matching ${sys} to the cloud: $(why_for "${sync_rc}" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')."
                        say_why "$(why_for "${sync_rc}")"
                    fi
                else
                    # The bytes the dry run counted, so the confirmation and
                    # the done page agree (the preview said 78 KB where the
                    # page then said 224 KB, 2026-09-07).
                    echo "${sys}|sync|${files}|${bytes}"
                fi
            ;;
            *)
                # match_plan_one prints none, remove or sync; anything else
                # is a failure to plan, and an announced item must not end
                # in silence.
                [ "${apply}" = "1" ] && echo "Couldn't check ${sys} against the cloud."
                log_message "match: no plan for ${sys} (${planned})"
                rc=1
            ;;
        esac
    done

    # The preview's plan, only when every system could be told: a preview
    # that could not see one system offers nothing to apply.
    if [ "${apply}" != "1" ] && [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ]; then
        if ! match_plan_write "${plan_lines}"; then
            echo "Couldn't keep track of what would change, so nothing can be removed yet. Try again."
            log_message "match: the plan could not be written to ${MATCH_PLAN}"
            rc=1
        fi
    fi

    if [ "${apply}" = "1" ]; then
        # ">>> removed 14|314572800|snes:12:300000000,gb:2:14572800" -- the
        # page renders it on its last screen. The counts are the files rclone
        # reports it removed, with the sizes listed before it ran (#308 gpt
        # F-CS-26); they were the preview's, and a system one of whose
        # deletions failed was reported as though all of them had happened.
        # --max-delete holds each system to the preview's count.
        echo ">>> removed ${total_removed}|${total_bytes}|${removed_detail}"
        log_message "match: applied, removed ${total_removed} files, rc=${rc}"
        tree_record_give
        # The page that ran it fades; the row in the menu has to be able to
        # answer "did that work?" afterwards, like every other cloud action.
        record_outcome content-match "${rc}"
    fi
    return ${rc}
    } 9>&-
}

content_files() {
    local dir="$1"; shift
    # One rule for both sides (D-CLOUD-048), set by MEDIA_MODE (D-CLOUD-050):
    #   roms  -- ROMs and BIOS only: the scraper's folders and the game list
    #            are neither listed nor moved
    #   with  -- ROMs and game content together
    #   only  -- game content alone: the scraper's folders and gamelist.xml
    # The game list is game content (D-CLOUD-049): the scraper writes it
    # beside the artwork, and a restored-then-scraped device must read as
    # matching its cloud under ROMs alone. At any depth, as the transfers
    # move it (the ROMs pass excludes "**/gamelist.xml", the game-list pass
    # includes it): a list below a system's own folder was counted as a ROM
    # (the audit of the fixes, G-A-10).
    local -a media=()
    local d
    case "${MEDIA_MODE:-roms}" in
        roms) for d in ${MEDIA_DIRS:-images videos manuals screenshots fanart boxart wheel mix maps media}; do media+=( ! -path "${dir%/}/${d}/*" ); done
              media+=( ! -name gamelist.xml ) ;;
        only) media+=( "(" -name gamelist.xml )
              for d in ${MEDIA_DIRS:-images videos manuals screenshots fanart boxart wheel mix maps media}; do media+=( -o -path "${dir%/}/${d}/*" ); done
              media+=( ")" ) ;;
    esac
    find "${dir}" -type f \
        ! -name '*.srm' ! -name '*.sav' ! -name '*.fs' ! -name '*.state*' \
        ! -name '*.auto' ! -name '*.dsv*' ! -name '*.eep' ! -name '*.mpk' \
        ! -name '*.sra' ! -name '*.fla' ! -name '*.mcd' ! -name '*.mcr' \
        ! -path '*/save/*' ! -path '*/memcards/*' \
        ! -path '*/shared/savefiles/*' ! -path '*/PPSSPP/*' \
        ! -path '*conflicted copy*' ! -name '*.sync-conflict-*' \
        ! -name '*.????????.partial' \
        ! -path "${dir%/}/README.txt" \
        "${media[@]}" "$@" 2>/dev/null
}
# Local systems that hold content, for the union scan.
local_content_dirs() {
    local d base
    for d in "${DEST}"/*/; do
        [ -d "${d}" ] || continue
        base=$(basename "${d}")
        case "${base}" in savefiles|savestates|screenshots|backup) continue ;; esac
        content_files "${d}" | head -1 | grep -q . && printf '%s\n' "${base}"
    done
}
# What a copy from side $1 to side $2 would move, as "count|bytes". Both
# files are "size|relpath" listings, and a line matches only when the far
# side has the same name at the same size -- so a file absent over there
# counts, and so does one present at a different size, which is what
# `rclone copy` compares (size, then modtime where the backend keeps one).
# A same-size file is NOT counted whatever changed inside it: these listings
# carry name and size only, so a file rewritten to the same length -- a
# patched ROM, a re-saved config -- reads as present, though a copy would
# move it on modtime or hash. The figure here can therefore run under what
# a copy moves, never over. The caller also strips the game list from both
# listings first (see --scan): its direction is decided by a modtime these
# listings do not carry, so a differing size is not a direction. The count
# and the bytes describe one set, so a page can put them on one line without
# contradicting itself; until 2026-09-08 the count compared names alone and
# would have read "0 FILES" beside a non-zero size for a ROM re-uploaded at
# a new size.
# Not comm(1): the image's busybox has no comm, and `comm ... | wc -l` then
# reads 0 -- "nothing differs" -- which is the wrong way for a count to fail
# (found in the VM, 2026-09-06). awk is what this script already runs on;
# the getline form is safe when either file is empty, where the NR==FNR
# idiom is not.
delta_of() {
    awk -F'|' -v L="$2" 'BEGIN { while ((getline x < L) > 0) a[x] = 1 }
        !($0 in a) { n++; b += $1 } END { print n+0 "|" b+0 }' "$1"
}
# Drop from a cloud "size|path" listing what content_files drops locally, so
# the two sides are counted by one rule.
#
# The same set content_files and the transfers describe (#308 gpt F-CS-30):
# a save folder at any depth -- save/, memcards/, PPSSPP/ and dc's
# shared/savefiles/, as the local find and the unanchored rclone excludes
# have them -- and the setup's note at a unit's root (a README.txt directly
# in a system's folder), which neither side carries. A README deeper in a
# game's folder is that game's, and is content on both sides. This used to
# look for save folders one level down only, missed shared/savefiles, and
# dropped every README at any depth, so a restored system read as differing
# from its own cloud copy.
cloud_content_filter() {
    local dirs; dirs="^($(echo ${MEDIA_DIRS} | tr ' ' '|'))$"
    awk -F'|' -v dirs="${dirs}" -v mode="${MEDIA_MODE}" '
        { n = split($2, seg, "/"); if (n < 2) next
          f = seg[n]
          game = (n > 2 && seg[2] ~ dirs) || f == "gamelist.xml"
          if (mode == "roms" && game) next
          if (mode == "only" && !game) next
          if (f ~ /\.(srm|sav|fs|auto|eep|mpk|sra|fla|mcd|mcr)$/ || f ~ /\.state/ || f ~ /\.dsv/) next
          if ($2 ~ /conflicted copy/ || f ~ /\.sync-conflict-/) next
          if (f ~ /\.[^.\/][^.\/][^.\/][^.\/][^.\/][^.\/][^.\/][^.\/]\.partial$/) next
          if (n == 2 && f == "README.txt") next
          for (i = 2; i < n; i++) {
              if (seg[i] == "save" || seg[i] == "memcards" || seg[i] == "PPSSPP") next
              if (seg[i] == "shared" && i + 1 < n && seg[i + 1] == "savefiles") next
          }
          print }'
}
# --with-media: include scraped game content (D-CLOUD-048). Off by default:
# the scraper's folders under a system are neither moved nor counted unless
# the switch is on, so a restored-then-scraped device does not read as
# "different" from its cloud copy. Taken from anywhere on the command line.
MEDIA_MODE=roms
_ARGS=()
for _a in "$@"; do
    case "${_a}" in
        --with-media) MEDIA_MODE=with ;;
        --media-only) MEDIA_MODE=only ;;
        *) _ARGS+=("${_a}") ;;
    esac
done
set -- "${_ARGS[@]}"
MEDIA_DIRS="images videos manuals screenshots fanart boxart wheel mix maps media"
# What the main rclone pass carries, per mode. The game list never rides the
# main pass: it has its own --update pass below (newest wins), which runs
# only when game content is in scope.
MEDIA_EXCLUDES=()
case "${MEDIA_MODE}" in
    roms) for _d in ${MEDIA_DIRS}; do MEDIA_EXCLUDES+=(--exclude "/${_d}/**"); done ;;
    only) for _d in ${MEDIA_DIRS}; do MEDIA_EXCLUDES+=(--include "/${_d}/**"); done ;;
esac

case "${1}" in
    --match)
        # Preview by default; --apply is what deletes.
        if [ "${2}" = "--apply" ]; then
            match_run 1
        else
            match_run 0
        fi
        exit $?
    ;;
    --scan)
        # One line per system in the union of cloud and device:
        #   name|cloud_bytes|supported|device_bytes|files_in_cloud_not_here|files_here_not_in_cloud|bytes_in_cloud_not_here|bytes_here_not_in_cloud
        # Both sides listed by the same rule (D-CLOUD-048) as "size|relpath"
        # and compared by name and size (delta_of), because totals cannot say
        # whether one side has what the other has. Fields 7 and 8 are what a
        # copy in that direction would send; fields 5 and 6 count the same
        # set. The game list is in the totals and never in the comparison
        # (below). They arrived 2026-09-08; the first six keep their position
        # and type, so a page built against six still reads this line.
        SUP=$(supported_systems)
        TMP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/cloud-scan.XXXXXX); trap 'rm -rf "${TMP}"' EXIT
        rclone lsf -R --files-only --format "sp" --separator "|" "${ROOT}ROMs/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null \
            | cloud_content_filter > "${TMP}/cloud"
        scan_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
        # A code other than 3 from a folder that is simply not there yet
        # (a server whose "missing" rclone does not map to "not found",
        # #142) is an empty cloud, not one that could not be read.
        if [ "${scan_rc}" -ne 0 ] && [ "${scan_rc}" -ne 3 ] && absent_not_broken "${ROOT}ROMs/"; then
            log_message "scan: ROMs is not there yet (rclone exit ${scan_rc}; its nearest listable parent lacks it)"
            scan_rc=3
        fi
        # BIOS is the ROMs tier's, never game content's: under --media-only it
        # is not listed, so the union does not carry a line the page would
        # skip and the log would puzzle over (3608 cloud BIOS files "not on
        # this device" under game content alone, RG35XX SP, 2026-09-06).
        if [ "${MEDIA_MODE}" != only ]; then
            rclone lsf -R --files-only --format "sp" --separator "|" "${ROOT}BIOS/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null \
                | grep -v '^[0-9]*|README\.txt$' | sed 's/|/|bios\//' >> "${TMP}/cloud"
            bios_rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
            if [ "${bios_rc}" -ne 0 ] && [ "${bios_rc}" -ne 3 ] && absent_not_broken "${ROOT}BIOS/"; then
                log_message "scan: BIOS is not there yet (rclone exit ${bios_rc}; its nearest listable parent lacks it)"
                bios_rc=3
            fi
            # Keep the code that says the most. A missing folder is rclone's
            # 3 and the one code an empty cloud gives, so a ROMs listing the
            # cloud refused (5, 7) must not be overwritten by a BIOS folder
            # that merely is not there yet.
            if [ "${bios_rc}" -ne 0 ] && { [ "${scan_rc}" -eq 0 ] || [ "${scan_rc}" -eq 3 ]; }; then
                scan_rc=${bios_rc}
            fi
        fi
        # A listing that failed with the network gone is not an empty cloud,
        # and the page must not be handed one: every system on the device

            # prefix is cut by length, not by pattern, so a system name

            # Under game content it travels in its own pass, --update, newest
            # wins (the transfer below); these listings carry no modtime to
            # say which side that is, so a size that differs is not a
            # direction, and a page that counted it read "1 FILE TO RESTORE"
            # on whichever side's list was older -- and kept reading it,
            # since a run moves nothing that way (found in review,
            # 2026-09-08). Any depth, as the transfer's "**/gamelist.xml".

            # there the strip touches only a list nested in a subfolder.

        # listed for size alone and never compared: device_bytes and every
        # comparison field are 0 without looking. The page reads an empty
        # far side as "all of it moves", which is the only true reading of

        all_listing() { # <path>: LISTED=its folders; the run stops when it cannot be read

#

# works before declaring success.

#   --info       key=value connection facts (IP, SSH command, override
#                state, password, sshd state, OAuth-port state,
#                configured remotes)

#                OAuth port 53682
#   --set-content-remote <path>  change the content root alone (CONTENT_REMOTE;
#                the chooser's, fork #352); nothing moves
#   --set-saves-remote <path>  change the cloud folder (SAVES_REMOTE) the sync
#                (--set-syncpath is accepted as the older spelling)
#                tools use, keeping SETTINGS_REMOTE alongside it; refuses a
#                path the remote cannot use
#   --accept-saves-root  the saves folder is on a different card than the last
#                sync and that is intended (cloud_saves_root)
#   --check-syncpath [path]  validate a cloud folder against the remote's
#                shape without changing anything (default: the current one)
#   --content-location  report where this device's ROMs/BIOS actually are in
#                the cloud (key=value; STATE=ok|stranded-at-root|empty;
#                unreadable, exit 1, when its value is not in a form the
#                sync reads)
#   --use-content-root  point content back at the remote root, moving nothing
#   --connected  exit 0 when an inbound SSH session is established, so the
#                connect step can be verified rather than taken on faith
#   --check [remote]  verify a remote (default: first); exit 0 working,
#                1 missing, 2 configured but unreachable

. /etc/profile

SCRIPT_NAME=$(basename "$0")
LOG_FILE="/var/log/cloud_sync.log"
SYNC_CONF="/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf"

log_message() {
    local message="$1"
    local timestamp=$(date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    echo "[${timestamp}] [INFO] [${SCRIPT_NAME}] ${message}" >> ${LOG_FILE}
}

# The config is shell: every cloud script sources it. So a value is written
# as text between double quotes, never through a sed replacement -- where &
# is the matched line and | ends the expression, so "/R&D/Saves" became
# garbage and "/a|b" failed the write while OK was printed (audit #307
# PL-051) -- and a value that would mean something to a shell between double
# quotes (" $ ` \) is refused where it is typed (syncpath_problem).
#
# conf_set KEY VALUE [KEY VALUE ...] writes every pair in one pass, each
# KEY= line replaced (every one, as the sed was) or appended, to a file
# beside the config that is renamed over it: all the keys or none, and the
# previous config intact when the write fails. The values reach awk through
# the environment, so nothing in them is interpreted. Returns non-zero when
# the config could not be written.
conf_set() {
    local tmp="${SYNC_CONF}.tmp.$$" src="${SYNC_CONF}" n=0 i
    local -a pairs=() want=()
    # Something at the config's path that is not a file is not a config this
    # can write: read as "absent", `mv -f` then put the new file INSIDE a
    # directory there and succeeded (audit of stream C, G-C-04).
    if [ -e "${SYNC_CONF}" ] && [ ! -f "${SYNC_CONF}" ]; then
        return 1
    fi
    [ -f "${src}" ] || src=/dev/null
    while [ $# -ge 2 ]; do
        n=$((n + 1)); pairs+=("CONF_K${n}=$1" "CONF_V${n}=$2")
        want+=("$1=\"$2\""); shift 2
    done
    # Braced, and silenced as a whole: a redirection that fails opening the
    # temp file happens before a `2>/dev/null` written after it, and the
    # shell printed its own diagnostic -- a line number and the temp file's
    # path -- ahead of the caller's sentence (G-C-07).
    if { env "${pairs[@]}" CONF_N="${n}" awk '
        BEGIN {
            n = ENVIRON["CONF_N"] + 0
            for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                k[i] = ENVIRON["CONF_K" i]
                line[i] = k[i] "=\"" ENVIRON["CONF_V" i] "\""
            }
        }
        {
            for (i = 1; i <= n; i++)
                if (index($0, k[i] "=") == 1) { print line[i]; seen[i] = 1; next }
            print
        }
        END { for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!seen[i]) print line[i] }
    ' "${src}" > "${tmp}" && mv -f "${tmp}" "${SYNC_CONF}"; } 2>/dev/null; then
        # Written is what the file says, not what mv returned: a regular
        # file at the path, holding every line asked for.
        [ -f "${SYNC_CONF}" ] || return 1
        for i in "${want[@]}"; do
            grep -qFx -- "${i}" "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null || return 1
        done
        return 0
    fi
    rm -f "${tmp}" 2>/dev/null
    return 1
}
