                    if (d == "\\") {
                        e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
                        if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
                        ok = 0
                        why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
                                        : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
                        break
                    }
                    if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
                    v = v d; i++
                }
                if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
                if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
            } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
                j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
                if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
            } else {
                match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
            }
            if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
            if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }
        }
        END {
            if (cntrl) { print "line " cntrl ": a control character other than a tab"; exit 2 }
            if (other) { print "line " other ": " k " set in a form this reader does not read"; exit 2 }
            if (found && !firstok) { print firstwhy; exit 2 }
            if (found) print first
        }
    ' ${SYNC_CONF}
}

# Wait for any confirm/cancel input: controller (evtest) or keyboard.
wait_for_button() {
    local input_device=""
    for dev in /dev/input/event*; do
        if [ -c "$dev" ]; then
            local supports=$(udevadm info "$dev" 2>/dev/null | awk '/ID_INPUT_JOYSTICK=1/ {print "joystick"}')
            if [ "$supports" = "joystick" ]; then
                input_device="$dev"
                break
            fi
        fi
    done
    if [ -n "$input_device" ]; then
        evtest "$input_device" 2>/dev/null | grep -m 1 -E "BTN_(SOUTH|EAST|A|B|START).*value 1" >/dev/null
    else
        read -sn1 2>/dev/null
    fi
}

# Connection facts, shared by the console flow and the native UI.
# resolve_connection sets SSH_CMD, SHOW_QR, OVERRIDE_ACTIVE and IP_ADDR
# (empty when offline).
resolve_connection() {
    OVERRIDE_ACTIVE=0
    IP_ADDR=$(ip route get 1 2>/dev/null | awk '{for (i=1;i<=NF;i++) if ($i=="src") {print $(i+1); exit}}')
    # The -L tunnel lets the provider sign-in page (which rclone serves on
    # the handheld at localhost:53682) open in the computer's own browser,
    # so the full 'auto config' flow works over SSH - see
    # rclone.org/remote_setup.
    SSH_CMD="ssh -L 53682:localhost:53682 root@${IP_ADDR}"
    SHOW_QR=1
    # Optional connection override: when the device is reached through a
    # gateway that remaps its address (development setups, tunnels,
    # proxies), the command in this file is shown instead of the direct one.
    OVERRIDE_FILE="/storage/.config/cloud_setup_ssh"
    if [ -s "${OVERRIDE_FILE}" ]; then
        SSH_CMD=$(head -n1 "${OVERRIDE_FILE}")
        SHOW_QR=0
        OVERRIDE_ACTIVE=1
        log_message "Using connection override: ${SSH_CMD}"
    fi
}

# True when at least one inbound SSH session is established (a peer is
# connected to local port 22). Reads /proc/net/tcp* directly so it works
# without ss/netstat; port 22 is 0016 hex, state 01 is ESTABLISHED.
ssh_session_established() {
    local f
    for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do
        [ -r "$f" ] || continue
        if awk 'NR>1 { n=split($2,a,":"); if (a[n]=="0016" && $4=="01") found=1 } END { exit found?0:1 }' "$f"; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# True when something on the device already listens on rclone's OAuth
# port 53682 (hex D1B2, state 0A is LISTEN) - a stale sign-in webserver
# from an interrupted `rclone config` would make the next auto-config
# attempt fail with "bind: address already in use".
auth_port_busy() {
    local f
    for f in /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6; do
        [ -r "$f" ] || continue
        if awk 'NR>1 { n=split($2,a,":"); if (a[n]=="D1B2" && $4=="0A") found=1 } END { exit found?0:1 }' "$f"; then
            return 0
        fi
    done
    return 1
}

# Does this cloud folder work on this remote?
#
# Dropbox, Google Drive and OneDrive are path-based: "/GAMES" is a folder and
# any name will do. S3, B2 and friends are bucket-based - the first path
# component IS the bucket, and bucket names have rules the shipped default
# breaks (uppercase is illegal), so a sync fails with InvalidBucketName and
# nothing in that message points back at this setting.
#
# rclone reports the distinction itself, so no provider list is hardcoded.
# Returns 0 when the path will work; prints a reason and returns 1 when not.
# Listings that decide something get a bound (as the sync scripts' do) -- the
# folder probe below and the parent walk alike; `backend features` asks
# rclone about itself and makes no round trip: a cloud that never answers is
# a refusal in 30 s, not a wizard that hangs. Until #151 PL-15 the probe was
# the one unbounded listing here, and this comment covered only the walk.
readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)
# Is this remote path missing, rather than unreadable? rclone answers "not
# found" (exit 3) when the server's reply is the one it maps to that, and a
# plain error (exit 1) when the words differ: an FTP server that answers a
# missing folder with 501 "No such directory." where the standard reply is
# 550 makes every "is it there yet?" branch read as "the cloud is broken"
# (#142, from the #133 matrix). The parent settles it, whatever the words:
# walk up until a level lists. A level that lists and lacks the next name is
# a path not created yet (0); one that lists and holds it means the failure
# was something else (1); a remote whose root will not list is broken (1).
# On a bucket an absent prefix lists as empty, which is the same answer
# (D-CLOUD-120). Called only after a listing has already failed with a code
# other than 3, so the everyday path costs nothing extra.
absent_not_broken() {
    local path="${1%/}" remote rel name parent listing
    remote="${path%%:*}:"; rel="${path#*:}"; rel="${rel#/}"
    while [ -n "${rel}" ]; do
        name="${rel##*/}"; parent="${rel%/*}"
        [ "${parent}" = "${rel}" ] && parent=""
        if listing=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "${remote}/${parent:+${parent}/}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
            printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- "${name}/" && return 1
            return 0
        fi
        [ -n "${parent}" ] || return 1
        rel="${parent}"
    done
    return 1
}

# Callers pass the first remote; an empty one stops after the string checks,
# which hold with no remote configured at all.
syncpath_problem() {
    local path="$1" remote="$2" bucket probe
    path="/$(echo "${path}" | sed 's:^/*::; s:/*$::')"

    if [ "${path}" = "/" ]; then
        echo "Your cloud folder can't be empty."
        return 1
    fi
    # The config is shell, sourced by every cloud script: the characters a
    # shell reads inside double quotes, and control characters, are refused
    # where the folder is typed (audit #307 PL-051, conf_set).
    case "${path}" in
        *[\"\$\`\\]*|*[[:cntrl:]]*)
            echo "Your cloud folder's name can't contain \", \$, \`, or \\."
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    # Every part of the path is a folder's name, and the checks below read
    # the text. A part that is empty (//), . or .. names no folder of its
    # own: /Mine/Backups/. is /Mine/Backups on a cloud that resolves it,
    # while its siblings -- <parent>/Backups and <parent>/Content, made from
    # the text by dirname -- came out as /Mine/Backups/Backups and
    # /Mine/Backups/Content, inside it: the nesting the sibling check below
    # exists to stop, walked past (the audit of the fix round, PL-009; gpt
    # G2-C-04). Refused where it is typed, before any other check reads the
    # text, with the folder the path would have meant.
    case "${path}/" in
        *//*|*/./*|*/../*)
            local part canon="" try
            local -a parts=()
            IFS=/ read -r -a parts <<< "${path#/}"
            for part in "${parts[@]}"; do
                case "${part}" in
                    ""|.) ;;
                    ..) canon="${canon%/*}" ;;
                    *) canon="${canon}/${part}" ;;
                esac
            done
            if [ -z "${canon}" ]; then
                echo "Your cloud folder can't be empty."
                return 1
            fi
            # Offered only as a folder the checks below take: two levels
            # at least, and not named like its own siblings.
            try="${canon}"
            case "${canon#/}" in */*) ;; *) try="${canon}/Saves" ;; esac
            case "$(printf '%s' "${try##*/}" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" in
                backups|content) try="${try%/*}/Saves" ;;
            esac
            echo "Your cloud folder can't have an empty part, or a part called . or .., in its path."
            echo "Try ${try}."
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    # Player-facing, these call it the cloud folder, which is what the
    # interface's row and its refusal dialog call it (G-C-03 claude).
    #
    # The saves folder has to sit inside another folder. Its settings
    # backups and games are kept beside it -- <parent>/Backups and
    # <parent>/Content -- and a saves folder at the top of the cloud has no
    # parent to keep them in. The setter used to put them INSIDE it instead
    # (/GAMES/Backups, /GAMES/Content): the nesting a mirror of the saves
    # folder deletes, because to the saves allowlist every file in them is
    # excluded (audit #307 PL-015, rclone-cloud-sync.md). So it is refused
    # where it is typed, with the folder to use instead -- on a bucket remote
    # that is the bucket and a folder in it, the shape the bucket message
    # below asks for anyway.
    case "${path#/}" in
        */*) ;;
        *)
            echo "Your cloud folder needs to sit inside another folder, so your settings backups and games can go beside it."
            echo "Try ${path}/Saves."
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    # And the three have to be three folders. The settings and content
    # folders are <parent>/Backups and <parent>/Content, so a saves folder
    # called Backups or Content is its own sibling: two tiers in one folder,
    # and the saves sync walking the other tier's files (audit #307, G-C-01).
    # Compared case-folded, because Dropbox and OneDrive fold case.
    local parent="${path%/*}" folded
    folded="$(printf '%s' "${path}" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
    local sibling=""
    [ "${folded}" = "$(printf '%s' "${parent}/Backups" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" ] && sibling="your settings backups"
    [ "${folded}" = "$(printf '%s' "${parent}/Content" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')" ] && sibling="your ROMs and BIOS"
    if [ -n "${sibling}" ]; then
        echo "Your cloud folder can't be called ${path##*/}: ${sibling} go in a folder of that name beside it."
        echo "Try ${parent}/Saves."
        return 1
    fi
    [ -n "${remote}" ] || return 0

    # No provider rules are encoded here on purpose. rclone does not validate
    # bucket names itself - it hands them to the provider and relays the
    # rejection - so the rules live with the provider, differ between them,
    # and would go stale in this script. The problem was never missing
    # validation; it was validation arriving at sync time, in a log, as
    # "InvalidBucketName" with nothing tying it to the folder that caused it.
    #
    # So: ask the provider now, and attach the answer to the setting.
    #
    # Only what rclone says went wrong, never its listing. This used to read
    # stdout as well, so a folder that already existed and held anything --
    # a saves folder with savestates/ in it, which is every folder somebody
    # would type on a second device -- was refused as "your provider would
    # not accept this folder", with the folder's own contents quoted as the
    # reason (found by the A3 fixture on the VM pair, 2026-09-06).
    probe=$(rclone lsd "${remote}${path#/}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" --log-level ERROR 2>&1 >/dev/null | head -2)
    case "${probe}" in
        # A folder that does not exist yet is fine - it gets created on use.
        *"not found"*|*NoSuchBucket*|"") return 0 ;;
    esac
    # The same folder, on a server whose "missing" rclone relays as a plain
    # error rather than "not found" (#142). On a path-based cloud a folder
    # its parent lacks is a folder not created yet, whatever the words. On
    # a bucket the first component is a bucket name the provider judges,
    # and the provider's own answer stands -- the parent rule would read
    # InvalidBucketName as "not there yet" and store the name it rejected.
    #
    # Which kind this remote is, rclone says in JSON, and the answer has to
    # be one of the two before anything rests on it. A `backend features`
    # that fails or prints neither is "unknown", and unknown takes the
    # provider's refusal at face value: the parent walk runs only on a
    # remote known to be path-based. Until #151 PL-14 a failed call read as
    # "not bucket-based" -- a grep over empty output -- and the walk ran,
    # so the one guard against storing a rejected bucket name fell open
    # exactly when rclone could not be asked.
    local features bucket_based=unknown
    if features=$(rclone backend features "${remote}" 2>/dev/null); then
        case "${features}" in
            *'"BucketBased": true'*)  bucket_based=yes ;;
            *'"BucketBased": false'*) bucket_based=no ;;
        esac
    fi
    if [ "${bucket_based}" = no ] && absent_not_broken "${remote}${path#/}"; then
        return 0
    fi

    # Something is wrong. If the remote is bucket-based, name the reason the
    # message will not: the first path component is a bucket, not a folder.
    if [ "${bucket_based}" = yes ]; then
        bucket="${path#/}"; bucket="${bucket%%/*}"
        echo "Your provider wouldn't accept \"${bucket}\"."
        echo
        echo "This provider keeps things in buckets, so the first part of the"
        echo "folder is a bucket name, not a folder - and bucket names have"
        echo "rules that folders do not. They are also shared with everyone"
        echo "else using the provider, not private to your account."
        echo
        echo "  ${probe}"
        echo
        echo "Try something like /pixelelated-saves-yourname/Saves instead."
    else
        echo "Your provider wouldn't accept this folder:"
        echo
        echo "  ${probe}"
    fi
    return 1
}

case "$1" in
    --info)
        # Machine-readable connection facts for the native UI.
        resolve_connection
        echo "IP=${IP_ADDR}"
        echo "SSH_CMD=${SSH_CMD}"
        echo "OVERRIDE=${OVERRIDE_ACTIVE}"
        # Whether a root password is set, never the password: this output is
        # parsed by EmulationStation through a pipeline, and a credential that
        # crosses a script boundary is one careless echo from a log (#116,
        # D-INFRA-008). The page that must show or pre-fill it reads
        # root.password in-process from its own settings.
        echo "PASSWORD_SET=$([ -n "$(get_setting root.password)" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
        echo "SSH_UP=$(systemctl is-active sshd 2>/dev/null)"
        echo "AUTH_PORT=$(auth_port_busy && echo busy || echo free)"
        # Both names for one value: EmulationStation reads SYNCPATH= until its
        # side of the vocabulary sweep (#73) lands; SAVES_REMOTE= is the name.
        # A folder in a form the scripts cannot read is named as none: the
        # sync refuses that config too, and the folder editor the interface
        # opens from this line is the way to set one it can (gpt G2-C-01).
        if ! saves_remote="$(conf_get SAVES_REMOTE)"; then
            log_message "SAVES_REMOTE in ${SYNC_CONF} is not in a form the sync reads (${saves_remote}); no folder named"
            saves_remote=""
        fi
        echo "SAVES_REMOTE=${saves_remote}"
        echo "SYNCPATH=${saves_remote}"
        echo "REMOTES=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
        # Which provider this device is actually connected to. The name is the
        # player's own label for the remote; the type is rclone's word for the
        # service (dropbox, drive, webdav...), which EmulationStation turns
        # into the name the player picked it by. Until this, nothing on any
        # screen said who the cloud was -- the setup page offered to connect
        # one and never mentioned the one already there (fork #110).
        remote_name="$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
        remote_name="${remote_name%:}"
        echo "REMOTE_NAME=${remote_name}"
        echo "REMOTE_TYPE=$(rclone config show "${remote_name}" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*type[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p' | head -1)"
        exit 0
    ;;
    --content-location)
        # Where is this device's content actually stored in the cloud?
        #
        # CONTENT_REMOTE is new, so an upgrading device gains one it never had.
        # Anyone who had put ROMs at the remote root by hand - the only way
        # content reached the cloud before f60ea2b8f8 - would find the content
        # list empty and nothing explaining why. Report the situation as
        # key=value so a UI can offer the choice rather than leaving the owner
        # to guess.
        #
        # Reported, never acted on: moving somebody's cloud files is not a
        # thing to do behind their back.
        REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
        [ -z "${REMOTE}" ] && { echo "STATE=no-remote"; exit 2; }
        if ! CP="$(conf_get CONTENT_REMOTE)"; then
            echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"
            echo "STATE=unreadable"
            exit 1
        fi

        # Share the restore scanner's local/supported membership, including
        # empty system directories. A backup's nonempty selection cannot
        # identify the games a fresh device is about to restore (#467).
        restore="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/cloud_content_restore"
        [ -x "${restore}" ] || restore=/usr/bin/cloud_content_restore
        if ! KNOWN=$("${restore}" --known-directories); then
            echo "STATE=unreadable"
            exit 1
        fi
        # A refused listing is not an empty folder. Preserve the provider's
        # code unless the existing parent walk proves the folder is absent.
        content_dirs() {
            local listing rc
            listing=$(rclone lsf --dirs-only "$1" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null)
            rc=$?
            if [ "${rc}" -ne 0 ]; then
                if [ "$1" != "${REMOTE}" ] && { [ "${rc}" -eq 3 ] || absent_not_broken "$1"; }; then
                    return 0
                fi
                return "${rc}"
            fi
            printf '%s\n' "${listing}"
        }
        content_members() {
            local d
            while IFS= read -r d; do
                d=${d%/}
                [ -n "${d}" ] || continue
                case "${d}" in
                    ROMs|BIOS) printf '%s\n' "${d}" ;;
                    *) printf '%s\n' "${KNOWN}" | grep -qxF -- "${d}" && printf '%s\n' "${d}" ;;
                esac
            done
            return 0
        }
        AT_PATH=0; AT_ROOT=0; ROOT_DIRS=""
        # Both listings carry the bound every listing here does (#308 claude
        # F-RS-13): rclone's own defaults are three runs of ten retries,
        # under a page waiting on the answer.
        if [ -n "${CP}" ]; then
            if ! LISTING=$(content_dirs "${REMOTE}${CP#/}"); then
                echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
                echo "STATE=unreadable"
                exit 1
            fi
            AT_PATH=$(printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | content_members | grep -c .)
        fi
        # A usable configured folder needs no account-root access. This also
        # works with providers granting access to only that prefix.
        if [ "${AT_PATH}" -eq 0 ]; then
            if ! LISTING=$(content_dirs "${REMOTE}"); then
                echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
                echo "STATE=unreadable"
                exit 1
            fi
            ROOT_DIRS=$(printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | content_members)
            AT_ROOT=$(printf '%s\n' "${ROOT_DIRS}" | grep -c .)
        fi

        # Where the games actually are, when the configured root holds nothing
        # of ours (fork #352, D-CLOUD-156): the cloud root's Content folder --
        # the saves folder's parent, /pixelelated/Content by default -- is
        # looked at for a ROMs or BIOS folder, and named, so the interface can
        # offer it before it asks the player to choose.
        FOUND=""
        if [ "${AT_PATH}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${AT_ROOT}" -eq 0 ]; then
            SV="$(conf_get SAVES_REMOTE)" || SV=""
            SV="${SV%/}"; SP="${SV%/*}"; [ "${SP}" = "${SV}" ] && SP=""
            CAND="${SP}/Content"
            if [ "${CAND}" != "${CP%/}" ]; then
                if ! LISTING=$(content_dirs "${REMOTE}${CAND#/}/"); then
                    echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
                    echo "STATE=unreadable"
                    exit 1
                fi
                if [ -n "$(printf '%s\n' "${LISTING}" | content_members)" ]; then
                    FOUND="${CAND}"
                fi
            fi
        fi
        if [ -n "${CP}" ] && [ "${AT_PATH}" -eq 0 ] && [ "${AT_ROOT}" -gt 0 ]; then
            FOUND=/
        fi
        echo "CONTENT_REMOTE=${CP}"
        echo "AT_PATH=${AT_PATH}"
        echo "AT_ROOT=${AT_ROOT}"
        echo "ROOT_DIRS=$(printf '%s\n' "${ROOT_DIRS}" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')"
        echo "FOUND=${FOUND}"
        # An empty CONTENT_REMOTE means the root IS the content path, so content
        # sitting there is correct rather than stranded - otherwise a UI would
        # keep offering to fix something already resolved.
        if [ -z "${CP}" ] && [ "${AT_ROOT}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "STATE=ok"
        elif [ "${AT_PATH}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "STATE=ok"
        elif [ "${AT_ROOT}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "STATE=stranded-at-root"
        elif [ -n "${FOUND}" ]; then
            echo "STATE=found-elsewhere"
        else
            echo "STATE=empty"
        fi
        exit 0
    ;;

    --set-content-remote)
        # Point this device's content root at a folder the player chose or
        # the scan found (the chooser, fork #352; CONTENT_REMOTE alone --
        # the saves and settings folders stay where they are). Moves
        # nothing, reversible, instant. The string checks are the saves
        # folder's: one leading slash, no unsafe shell syntax or traversal
        # components. Spaces, apostrophes and dots inside a name are ordinary
        # filename characters, passed literally by conf_set. A folder at the top of the
        # cloud is fine here, unlike a saves folder (it has no siblings).
        NEWPATH="$2"
        [ -z "${NEWPATH}" ] && { echo "ERROR empty path"; exit 1; }
        # Reject controls before command substitution can strip a trailing
        # newline and turn an invalid name into a different valid one.
        case "${NEWPATH}" in
            *[\$\`\\\"]*|*[[:cntrl:]]*) echo "That folder name has characters your cloud sync settings can't hold."; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        NEWPATH="/$(printf '%s' "${NEWPATH}" | sed 's:^/*::; s:/*$::')"
        case "${NEWPATH}" in
            "/") echo "ERROR root path not allowed"; exit 1 ;;
            */../*|*/..|*/./*|*/.|*//*) echo "That folder name can't be used."; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        if ! conf_set CONTENT_REMOTE "${NEWPATH}"; then
            echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be saved."
            log_message "Content path NOT changed to ${NEWPATH}: ${SYNC_CONF} could not be written"
            exit 1
        fi
        log_message "Content path set to ${NEWPATH} by request"
        echo "OK ${NEWPATH}"
        exit 0
    ;;
    --use-content-root)
        # The safe resolution: point this device back at the root where its
        # content already is. Moves nothing, reversible, instant.
        if ! conf_set CONTENT_REMOTE ""; then
            echo "ERROR the cloud sync settings could not be saved"
            log_message "Content path NOT changed: ${SYNC_CONF} could not be written"
            exit 1
        fi
        log_message "Content path set to the remote root by request"
        echo "OK content stays at the remote root"
        exit 0
    ;;

    --accept-saves-root)
        # The owner says the card the saves folder is on now is the right
        # one (#83): remember it, so saves transfers stop refusing.
        tool="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/cloud_saves_root"
        [ -x "${tool}" ] || tool=/usr/bin/cloud_saves_root
        exec "${tool}" accept
    ;;
    --check-syncpath)
        # Validate a candidate cloud folder without changing anything, so the
        # UI can refuse a bad one where it is typed rather than letting it
        # fail later inside a sync.
        if [ -n "${2:-}" ]; then
            CAND="$2"
        elif ! CAND="$(conf_get SAVES_REMOTE)"; then
            echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be read."
            exit 1
        else
            # The conf's own value is judged as the migration judges it
            # (the audit of the fixes, claude G3-D-07): one trailing slash
            # is a spelling, not an empty part.
            CAND="${CAND%/}"
        fi
        REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
        if [ -z "${REMOTE}" ]; then
            echo "No cloud remote configured."
            exit 2
        fi
        if syncpath_problem "${CAND}" "${REMOTE}"; then
            echo "OK ${CAND}"
            exit 0
        fi
        exit 1
    ;;

    --set-saves-remote|--set-syncpath)
        # Change the cloud folder the saves live in, and move the settings
        # backups and the ROMs with it -- as SIBLINGS, never inside it.
        # This used to write SETTINGS_REMOTE="<saves>/backup", which is the
        # first-layout nesting cloud_migrate_layout exists to undo and the
        # trap cloud_backup warns about: a mirror of the saves folder can
        # delete the archives kept beneath it. The siblings are the saves
        # folder's parent's: <parent>/Backups and <parent>/Content. A saves
        # folder at the top of the cloud has no parent and is refused
        # (syncpath_problem) -- it used to adopt the folder itself as the
        # parent, which nested both inside it (audit #307 PL-015).
        NEWPATH="$2"
        if [ -z "${NEWPATH}" ]; then
            echo "ERROR empty path"
            exit 1
        fi
        # Normalize: exactly one leading slash, no trailing slash.
        NEWPATH="/$(echo "${NEWPATH}" | sed 's:^/*::; s:/*$::')"
        if [ "${NEWPATH}" = "/" ]; then
            echo "ERROR root path not allowed"
            exit 1
        fi
        # Refuse a path this remote cannot use, rather than storing it and
        # letting the next sync fail with a provider error naming nothing the
        # player recognises. The string checks -- a parent for the siblings
        # (PL-015), no shell characters (PL-051) -- hold with no remote.
        SP_REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
        if ! syncpath_problem "${NEWPATH}" "${SP_REMOTE}"; then
            exit 1
        fi
        SP_PARENT="$(dirname "${NEWPATH}")"
        # All three or none (conf_set): a folder half-changed is a saves
        # folder whose settings still go to the old place.
        if ! conf_set SAVES_REMOTE "${NEWPATH}" \
                      SETTINGS_REMOTE "${SP_PARENT}/Backups" \
                      CONTENT_REMOTE "${SP_PARENT}/Content"; then
            # Under the interface's "THE CLOUD FOLDER WAS NOT CHANGED": this line
            # says why, and nothing the title already said (G-C-03 claude).
            echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be saved."
            log_message "Sync path NOT changed to ${NEWPATH}: ${SYNC_CONF} could not be written"
            exit 1
        fi
        log_message "Sync path changed to ${NEWPATH}"
        echo "OK ${NEWPATH}"
        exit 0
    ;;
    --free-auth-port)
        # Clear a stale sign-in webserver left by an interrupted
        # `rclone config`, so the next auto-config attempt can bind.
        pkill -f "rclone config" 2>/dev/null
        pkill -f "rclone authorize" 2>/dev/null
        log_message "Cleared stale processes holding the OAuth port"
        echo "OK"
        exit 0
    ;;
    --connected)
        # The native UI gates its connect step on this, so the player
        # cannot advance without an SSH session actually being open.
        if ssh_session_established; then
            echo "CONNECTED"
            exit 0
        fi
        echo "NONE"
        exit 1
    ;;
    --seed-folders)
        # Give a new remote a shape, so somebody with a fresh handheld can see
        # where their files go.
        #
        # Until the first upload these folders do not exist, so a player who
        # wants to seed their library from a computer first has to guess three
        # names and a per-system convention. The folders answer that; the
        # README in each answers what belongs there.
        #
        # The READMEs are also what makes this work at all on bucket-based
        # remotes (S3, B2): there the first path component is a bucket and the
        # rest is a key prefix, so an empty directory does not persist and
        # `rclone mkdir` on a subpath succeeds while creating nothing. A file
        # in the folder is what materialises it.
        #
        # Nothing is ever overwritten and nothing is deleted. Paths come from
        # the config, so a player who moved their cloud folder gets their own
        # layout seeded rather than ours.
        REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
        [ -z "${REMOTE}" ] && { echo "ERROR no remote"; exit 2; }
        # The folder is settled before anything is made
        # (cloud_migrate_layout --settle, D-CLOUD-169). A fresh install, or
        # a carried /GAMES, beside a fleet still on the earlier folder joins
        # it: seeding an empty /pixelelated beside the player's saves left a
        # new device reading a folder with none of them in it (the
        # mixed-installation test, D-CLOUD-158), and seeding the carried
        # /GAMES put a README there that every later check read as saves. A
        # carried default with nothing anywhere is pointed at the current
        # folders, which the seeding makes, as for any new cloud. A settle
        # that could not answer makes nothing. The wizard may still finish;
        # its boot step retries, without a misleading README at the old root.
        layout_tool="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/cloud_migrate_layout"
        [ -x "${layout_tool}" ] || layout_tool=/usr/bin/cloud_migrate_layout
        if [ ! -x "${layout_tool}" ]; then
            log_message "Seeding: cloud folder settlement is unavailable; nothing was made"
            exit 1
        fi
        settlement=$(timeout 30 "${layout_tool}" --settle 2>&1); settle_rc=$?
        case "${settle_rc}" in
            0) log_message "Seeding: this device's cloud folder was settled first (cloud_migrate_layout --settle)" ;;
            3) ;; # A current, populated, custom or kept folder needs no transition.
            *) log_message "Seeding: cloud folder settlement exited ${settle_rc}; nothing was made"
               settle_why=$(printf '%s\n' "${settlement}" | sed -n 's/^>>> why //p' | tail -1)
               if [ -n "${settle_why}" ]; then
                   echo ">>> why ${settle_why}"
               elif [ "${settle_rc}" -eq 124 ]; then
                   echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
               else
                   echo ">>> why YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
               fi
               echo "Your cloud folder couldn't be checked, so no folders were made. Try again."
               exit "${settle_rc}" ;;
        esac
        # Read as text, never eval'd: the config is shell, and a value an
        # earlier build wrote could carry a command (PL-051). A folder in a
        # form the scripts cannot read makes nothing: read as empty, it
        # became the default folder here and was seeded in the player's
        # cloud (gpt G2-C-01).
        if ! SAVES_REMOTE="$(conf_get SAVES_REMOTE)" \
           || ! SETTINGS_REMOTE="$(conf_get SETTINGS_REMOTE)" \
           || ! CONTENT_REMOTE="$(conf_get CONTENT_REMOTE)"; then
            echo "Your cloud sync settings couldn't be read, so no folders were made."
            log_message "Seeding: a folder in ${SYNC_CONF} is not in a form the sync reads; nothing was made"
            exit 1
        fi
        SAVES="${SAVES_REMOTE:-/pixelelated/Saves}"
        BACKUPS="${SETTINGS_REMOTE:-/pixelelated/Backups}"
        # An empty CONTENT_REMOTE is not a missing one: it is
        # --use-content-root's "the cloud's root", which is where the
        # content scripts put ROMs/ and BIOS/ (ROOT="<remote>:"). Only a
        # config with no such line gets the default (#308 gpt F-RS-20).
        if grep -q '^CONTENT_REMOTE=' "${SYNC_CONF}" 2>/dev/null; then
            CONTENT="${CONTENT_REMOTE%/}"
        else
            CONTENT="/pixelelated/Content"
        fi

        for d in "${SAVES}" "${SAVES}/savefiles" "${SAVES}/savestates" \
                 "${SAVES}/screenshots" "${BACKUPS}" \
                 ${CONTENT:+"${CONTENT}"} "${CONTENT}/ROMs" "${CONTENT}/BIOS"; do
            # --s3-directory-markers writes a zero-byte object ending in "/",
            # which is how S3 itself represents a folder -- without it a
            # bucket remote silently keeps nothing, and mkdir still exits 0.
            # Ignored by path-based backends, so it costs nothing there.
            # Bounded like the listings (#308 claude F-RS-13, gpt F-RS-19):
            # up to two dozen calls under one 90 s box in the interface.
            rclone mkdir --s3-directory-markers "${REMOTE}${d}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null
        done
        # The layout marker (fork #356): one line at the parent of the saves
        # folder saying which shape of folders this cloud carries, read by
        # every device before it offers a move or a creation
        # (cloud_migrate_layout --state). Written here because seeding is
        # where a cloud first takes the current shape.
        # Not beside a folder this project once shipped as its default: a
        # device that joined one marks nothing, and a layout=2 marker at
        # /ROCKNIX would say a thing about that cloud that is not so.
        # The same version-aware writer owns publication for migration and
        # seeding. Custom and earlier layouts publish no current marker.
        "${layout_tool}" --write-marker; marker_rc=$?
        case "${marker_rc}" in
            0|3) ;;
            *) log_message "Seeding: layout marker publication failed (${marker_rc})"
               exit "${marker_rc}" ;;
        esac

        seed_note() {
            local dir="$1" listing tmp; shift
            # Never clobber a note the owner may have written themselves, and
            # never write on a guess. The folder's own listing says whether a
            # README.txt is in it. Asking for the file by name could not: a
            # listing that failed for any reason read as "absent" and the
            # owner's note was replaced (audit #307 PL-047), and on a bucket
            # a key that is not there lists as nothing with exit 0, which read
            # as "present" -- so no README was ever written there (#308
            # claude F-RS-09). A listing that fails writes nothing.
            if ! listing=$(rclone lsf --files-only "${REMOTE}${dir}/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null); then
                log_message "Seeding: ${dir} could not be listed, so its README was not written"
                return 1
            fi
            printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | grep -qFx -- 'README.txt' && return 0
            tmp=$(mktemp) || return 1
            printf '%s\n' "$@" > "${tmp}"
            # --ignore-existing: another device may have written one since
            # the listing.
            rclone copyto --ignore-existing "${tmp}" "${REMOTE}${dir}/README.txt" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null
            rm -f "${tmp}"
        }

        seed_note "${SAVES}" \
            "Game saves, save states, and screenshots." \
            "" \
            "  savefiles/    battery saves" \
            "  savestates/   save state snapshots" \
            "  screenshots/" \
            "" \
            "The handheld writes these itself. Nothing to put here by hand."

        seed_note "${BACKUPS}" \
            "Settings backups, one folder per handheld." \
            "" \
            "Written by the device. Nothing to put here by hand."

        # Not at the top of somebody's cloud: with content at the root, the
        # ROMs and BIOS folders carry their own notes and the root keeps
        # whatever the owner has there.
        [ -n "${CONTENT}" ] && seed_note "${CONTENT}" \
            "Put your games and BIOS files here." \
            "" \
            "  ROMs/       one folder per system - snes, psx, n64, gba, ..." \
            "  BIOS/       BIOS and firmware files" \
            "" \
            "The handheld reads these when you choose" \
            "\"Restore from the cloud\" on it."

        seed_note "${CONTENT}/ROMs" \
            "Your games, one folder per system." \
            "" \
            "Use the same folder names the handheld uses - snes, psx, n64," \
            "gba, megadrive, and so on. The game list on the device shows them."

        seed_note "${CONTENT}/BIOS" \
            "BIOS and firmware files." \
            "" \
            "These land in /storage/roms/bios on the handheld, keeping" \
            "whatever subfolder structure you use here."

        # Report what is actually there, not what we asked for: on a bucket
        # remote a mkdir can succeed and leave nothing behind.
        for d in "${SAVES}" "${BACKUPS}" "${CONTENT}/ROMs" "${CONTENT}/BIOS"; do
            # A listing, never lsjson --stat: on a bucket remote stat reports
            # success for any path at all, so the MISSING branch could never
            # be reached -- the report would have been unconditionally OK,
            # which is the shape of an assertion that cannot fail.
            if [ -n "$(rclone lsf "${REMOTE}${d}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | head -1)" ] \
               || rclone lsf --dirs-only "${REMOTE}${d%/*}/" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | grep -qFx -- "${d##*/}/"; then
                echo "OK ${d}"
            else
                echo "MISSING ${d}"
            fi
        done
        exit 0
    ;;

    --check)
        # Verify a remote ($2 if given, else the first configured one);
        # plain-text verdict on stdout, exit 0 = working, 1 = missing,
        # 2 = configured but unreachable.
        REMOTE="$2"
        [ -z "${REMOTE}" ] && REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
        if [ -z "${REMOTE}" ]; then
            echo "NONE"
            log_message "Cloud setup check: no remotes configured"
            exit 1

        # The probe is bounded like every other listing here (RCLONE_LIST_OPTS:
        # one run, three low-level retries). It carried only the two timeouts,
        # so rclone's own defaults applied -- three runs of ten retries each --
        # under a blocking spinner on three interface pages; the shape #113

        if rclone lsd "${REMOTE}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "OK ${REMOTE}"
            log_message "Cloud setup verified working remote: ${REMOTE}"
            exit 0
        fi
        echo "FAIL ${REMOTE}"
        log_message "Cloud setup: remote ${REMOTE} failed verification"
        exit 2
    ;;
esac

# cloud_scan - what the cloud holds for this device, before anything is offered.
#
# The transfer pages scan first and offer only what the scan found
# (D-CLOUD-156, fork #350): the folder's state, the settings archives by
# device label, where the content is, and -- once the player has ticked
# what to move -- the content listing in those classes. This runs those
# reads and talks to the scan page in the protocol every cloud page reads
# (">>> unit", ">>> doing", ">>> why"), writing each result to a file the
# options page builds from.
#
#   cloud_scan                   the opening scan: the folder, the settings
#                                archives, where the content is (three items)
#   cloud_scan --content [--with-media|--media-only]
#                                the content listing for the systems page,
#                                in the classes ticked (one item)
#   cloud_scan --folder          the folder alone, for the cloud folder step
#                                at the end of cloud setup and at boot
#                                (D-CLOUD-170, fork #363; one item)
#
# Reads, with two exceptions, both settings: a fresh install beside a fleet
# still on an earlier folder joins it (cloud_migrate_layout --join), and a
# device on a superseded folder whose current folder another device has
# already made is re-pointed to it (cloud_migrate_layout --follow;
# D-CLOUD-160's "your other devices will follow"). Nothing in the cloud
# changes, so no lock is taken and a sync may run beside it.
#
# Results, under /storage/.cache/cloud_sync/scan/:
#   state             cloud_migrate_layout --state, one fact per line
#   archives          every settings archive in the Backups folder, one per line
#   settings          LABEL= (this device's), MINE= (its newest), NEWEST= (overall), COUNT=
#   content-location  cloud_setup --content-location, key=value
#   root-dirs         the folders at the cloud's root, one per line (the chooser's)
#   done              the epoch the opening scan completed; absent while it runs or failed
#   scan              cloud_content_restore --scan's rows        (--content)
#   systems           the systems this device syncs (--systems)  (--content)
#   content-done      the epoch the content scan completed       (--content)
#
# Exit: 0 all read; 69 no network (the page says SKIPPED - YOU'RE NOT
# ONLINE); 1 no cloud storage set up; otherwise the failing read's code,
# with a ">>> why" in the player's words before it (D-UI-028).

. /etc/profile 2>/dev/null

OUT=/storage/.cache/cloud_sync/scan
SYNC_CONF=/storage/.config/cloud_sync.conf
readonly EXIT_NO_NETWORK=69
# Every listing here is bounded as the other readers' are (#308 claude F-RS-13).
readonly -a RCLONE_LIST_OPTS=(--contimeout 15s --timeout 30s --low-level-retries 3 --retries 1)

say() { echo "$@"; }
log() { logger -t cloud_scan "$*" 2>/dev/null; }
why() { echo ">>> why $*"; }

# The shared reader (cloud_setup's, the content scripts', D-CLOUD-149): a
# value in a form the sync does not read is nothing here, never a folder.
conf_get() { # <KEY> (the content scripts' reader, mirrored so every reader agrees, D-CLOUD-149): its value, quotes off; nothing when absent; exit 2 when unreadable, and why on stdout
    [ -f ${SYNC_CONF} ] || return 0
    awk -v k="$1" '
        { t = $0; gsub(/\t/, "", t); if (t ~ /[[:cntrl:]]/ && !cntrl) cntrl = NR }
        index($0, k "=") != 1 && !other \
            && $0 ~ ("^[ \t]*((export|declare|typeset|readonly|local)([ \t]+-[A-Za-z]+)*[ \t]+)?" k "[ \t]*[+]?=") { other = NR }
        index($0, k "=") == 1 {
            s = substr($0, length(k) + 2); v = ""; r = ""; ok = 1; why = ""
            c = substr(s, 1, 1)
            if (c == "\"") {
                # Inside double quotes bash reads \" \\ \$ and \` as the one
                # character each (PL-015), and so does this; an unescaped $
                # or backtick is an expansion this reader does not make, and
                # any other backslash is refused as conf_valid refuses it.
                n = length(s); i = 2; closed = 0
                while (i <= n) {
                    d = substr(s, i, 1)
                    if (d == "\"") { closed = 1; break }
                    if (d == "\\") {
                        e = substr(s, i + 1, 1)
                        if (e == "\"" || e == "\\" || e == "$" || e == "`") { v = v e; i += 2; continue }
                        ok = 0
                        why = (e == "") ? "a value continued onto the next line, which this reader does not follow" \
                                        : "a backslash inside double quotes that is not one of the escapes bash reads there"
                        break
                    }
                    if (d == "$" || d == "`") { ok = 0; why = "a $ or a backtick inside double quotes"; break }
                    v = v d; i++
                }
                if (ok && !closed) { ok = 0; why = "a double-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
                if (ok) r = substr(s, i + 1)
            } else if (c == "'"'"'") {
                j = index(substr(s, 2), c)
                if (j) { v = substr(s, 2, j - 1); r = substr(s, j + 2) } else { ok = 0; why = "a single-quoted value that does not close on its line" }
            } else {
                match(s, /^[A-Za-z0-9_.\/:@%+,=-]*/); v = substr(s, 1, RLENGTH); r = substr(s, RLENGTH + 1)
            }
            if (ok && r !~ /^([ \t]+(#.*)?)?$/) { ok = 0; why = "something after the value that is not a # comment" }
            if (!found) { found = 1; first = v; firstok = ok; firstwhy = "line " NR ": " why }
        }
        END {
            if (cntrl) { print "line " cntrl ": a control character other than a tab"; exit 2 }
            if (other) { print "line " other ": " k " set in a form this reader does not read"; exit 2 }
            if (found && !firstok) { print firstwhy; exit 2 }
            if (found) print first
        }
    ' ${SYNC_CONF}
}

sibling() { # <name>: the script beside this one, else the installed one
    local t; t="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/$1"
    [ -x "${t}" ] || t="/usr/bin/$1"
    echo "${t}"
}
device_label() {
    local tool; tool=$(sibling cloud_device_id)
    [ -x "${tool}" ] && "${tool}" --label 2>/dev/null | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9_-'
}
os_name() {
    local name="${OS_NAME}"
    [ -z "${name}" ] && name=$(sed -n 's/^OS_NAME="\{0,1\}\([^"]*\)"\{0,1\}$/\1/p' /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    [ -z "${name}" ] && name="ROCKNIX"
    printf '%s\n' "${name}" | tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9_-'
}

# What an rclone exit means to a player: the sentences the card and the
# rows already carry for these codes (ThreadedCloudSync::whyForCode), so
# one code is never called two things and the French reaches them.
why_for_rc() {
    case "$1" in
        3|4) why "COULDN'T FIND YOUR CLOUD FOLDER" ;;
        5|124) why "YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING" ;;   # 124: a bounded step's timeout (the join)
        7|8) why "YOUR CLOUD WOULDN'T TAKE THE FILES" ;;
        *)   why "SOMETHING WENT WRONG" ;;
    esac
}

# Before any read: a place to write, a route, a remote.
prepare() {
    mkdir -p "${OUT}" || { log "scan: cannot make ${OUT}"; why "SOMETHING WENT WRONG"; exit 1; }
    # No route, nothing tried: the page says SKIPPED - YOU'RE NOT ONLINE from
    # the code alone (D-CLOUD-072, D-CLOUD-112).
    if ! ip route show default 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
        log "scan: no default route; skipped"
        exit "${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}"
    fi
    REMOTE=$(rclone listremotes 2>/dev/null | head -1)
    if [ -z "${REMOTE}" ]; then
        why "YOUR CLOUD STORAGE ISN'T SET UP YET"
        exit 1
    fi
}

# A read that failed ends the run with its why; 69 is the page's own sentinel.
stop_on() { # <rc> <what> [application output file]
    [ "$1" -eq 0 ] && return 0
    log "scan: $2 exited $1"
    [ "$1" -eq "${EXIT_NO_NETWORK}" ] && exit "$1"
    if [ -n "${3:-}" ]; then
        local reason
        reason=$(sed -n 's/^>>> why //p' "$3" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
        if [ -n "${reason}" ]; then
            why "${reason}"
        elif [ "$1" -eq 124 ]; then
            why "YOUR CLOUD STOPPED ANSWERING"
        else
            # Application codes are not rclone's codes. A refused layout
            # or invalid record does not mean that a folder is missing.
            why "YOUR CLOUD FOLDER COULDN'T BE READ"
        fi
    else
        why_for_rc "$1"
    fi
    exit "$1"
}

# --content: the listing the systems page is built from, in the classes
# the player ticked (cloud_content_restore --scan's own flags), and the
# systems this device syncs. One item; the page's row 3 says it is
# comparing.
scan_content() {
    local label="ROMS AND BIOS" rc
    case " $* " in
        *" --with-media "*) label="ROMS, BIOS, AND GAME CONTENT" ;;
        *" --media-only "*) label="GAME CONTENT" ;;
    esac
    rm -f "${OUT}"/scan "${OUT}"/scan.err "${OUT}"/systems "${OUT}"/content-done
    prepare
    echo ">>> unit ${label}||"
    echo ">>> doing compare"
    "$(sibling cloud_content_restore)" --scan "$@" > "${OUT}/scan" 2> "${OUT}/scan.err"; rc=$?
    [ "${rc}" -eq 0 ] || log "scan: --scan $* exited ${rc}: $(head -1 "${OUT}/scan.err" 2>/dev/null)"
    stop_on "${rc}" "--scan"
    "$(sibling cloud_content_restore)" --systems > "${OUT}/systems" 2>/dev/null || : > "${OUT}/systems"
    date +%s > "${OUT}/content-done"
    log "scan: content done ($(grep -c . "${OUT}/scan") rows, ${label})"
    exit 0
}

# 1. The folder: current, kept, superseded or the player's own; the current
#    folder's presence; the marker (cloud_migrate_layout --state, fork #353).
#    The opening scan's first item, and the whole of --folder.
read_folder() {
    local layout rc
    echo ">>> unit CLOUD FOLDER||"
    echo ">>> doing scan"
    layout=$(sibling cloud_migrate_layout)
    # A fresh install beside a fleet still on the earlier folder joins it first
    # (cloud_migrate_layout --join, a setting): the state below then reads the
    # folder the player's saves are in, and the move is offered from there
    # rather than CREATE IT beside them. 3 is "nothing to join"; anything else
    # that is not 0 is the cloud not answering, and stops the scan with its why.
    timeout 20 "${layout}" --join > "${OUT}/join" 2>&1; rc=$?
    case "${rc}" in
        0) log "scan: joined the fleet's earlier folder" ;;
        3) ;;
        *) stop_on "${rc}" "--join" "${OUT}/join" ;;
    esac
    "${layout}" --state > "${OUT}/state" 2>/dev/null; stop_on $? "--state" "${OUT}/state"
    # A device left on a superseded folder with nothing in it, whose current
    # folder another device has already made, follows the fleet here -- the
    # one place it does since no sync asks any more (D-CLOUD-170): the dialogs
    # then never ask about a folder the player has already answered for
    # elsewhere.
    if [ "$(sed -n 's/^STATE=//p' "${OUT}/state")" = superseded-empty ] \
       && [ "$(sed -n 's/^CURRENT_EXISTS=//p' "${OUT}/state")" = 1 ]; then
        timeout 20 "${layout}" --follow > "${OUT}/follow" 2>&1; rc=$?
        case "${rc}" in
            0) log "scan: followed the fleet to the current layout" ;;
            3) ;; # The remote may have changed since the state read; read it again.
            *) stop_on "${rc}" "--follow" "${OUT}/follow" ;;
        esac
        "${layout}" --state > "${OUT}/state" 2>/dev/null; stop_on $? "--state" "${OUT}/state"
    fi
}

case "$1" in
    --content) shift; scan_content "$@" ;;
    --folder)
        # The step reads state alone; the opening scan's other files are
        # left as they were, and are rewritten by the next opening scan.
        rm -f "${OUT}"/state
        prepare
        read_folder
        log "scan: folder done ($(sed -n 's/^STATE=//p' "${OUT}/state"))"
        exit 0 ;;
    "") ;;
    *) echo "usage: cloud_scan [--content [--with-media|--media-only] | --folder]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

rm -f "${OUT}"/state "${OUT}"/archives "${OUT}"/settings "${OUT}"/content-location "${OUT}"/root-dirs "${OUT}"/done
prepare
date +%s > "${OUT}/started"
read_folder

# 2. The settings archives, by the device that wrote each (the label in the
#    name, cloud_restore's rule): this device's newest first, else the newest
#    overall, else none -- the row is offered or dimmed from this (D-CLOUD-162).
echo ">>> unit SETTINGS BACKUPS||"
echo ">>> doing scan"
settings_remote=$(conf_get SETTINGS_REMOTE) || { why "YOUR CLOUD SYNC SETTINGS COULDN'T BE READ"; exit 1; }
settings_remote="${settings_remote%/}"
# Use the restore reader's directory priority, including inherited device IDs.
archive_tool=$(sibling rasteratops-settings-archive)
[ -r "${archive_tool}" ] || { why "SOMETHING WENT WRONG"; exit 1; }
. "${archive_tool}"
select_settings_archives "${REMOTE}${settings_remote}" "$(sibling cloud_device_id)"; rc=$?
stop_on "${rc}" "archives listing"
listing="${SETTINGS_ARCHIVE_LISTING}"
printf '%s\n' "${listing}" | sed '/^$/d' > "${OUT}/archives"
label=$(device_label); osn=$(os_name); mine=""; newest=""
if [ -n "${label}" ]; then
    mine=$(grep -E "^[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{6}-${label}-(${osn}|ROCKNIX|RASTERATOPS)_SETTINGS\.tar\.gz$" "${OUT}/archives" | sort | tail -1)
fi
newest=$(grep -E '^[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}_[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{6}-' "${OUT}/archives" | sort | tail -1)
{
    echo "SOURCE=${SETTINGS_ARCHIVE_SOURCE}"
    echo "LABEL=${label}"
    echo "MINE=${mine}"
    echo "NEWEST=${newest}"
    echo "COUNT=$(grep -c . "${OUT}/archives")"
} > "${OUT}/settings"

# 3. Where the content is: the configured root, the cloud root's
#    /Rasteratops/Content, or nowhere yet (cloud_setup --content-location,
#    fork #352) -- and the folders at the cloud's root, for the chooser the
#    page offers when nothing of ours is found. The listing itself waits for
#    --content, once the player has said which classes to compare.
echo ">>> unit GAME CONTENT||"
echo ">>> doing scan"
"$(sibling cloud_setup)" --content-location > "${OUT}/content-location" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
stop_on "${rc}" "--content-location" "${OUT}/content-location"
rclone lsf --dirs-only "${REMOTE}" "${RCLONE_LIST_OPTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | sed 's:/$::; /^$/d' > "${OUT}/root-dirs"; rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
stop_on "${rc}" "root listing"

date +%s > "${OUT}/done"
log "scan: done ($(grep -c . "${OUT}/archives") archives, $(sed -n 's/^STATE=//p' "${OUT}/state"), content $(sed -n 's/^STATE=//p' "${OUT}/content-location"))"
exit 0

    cp -a ${PKG_BUILD}/emulationstation ${INSTALL}/usr/bin

    ln -sf /storage/.cache/system_timezone ${INSTALL}/etc/timezone

    ln -sf /storage/.config/emulationstation/themes ${INSTALL}/etc/emulationstation/themes
    ln -sf ${INSTALL}/usr/config/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg ${INSTALL}/etc/emulationstation/es_systems.cfg

                <extension>.sh</extension>
                <command>%ROM%</command>
                <platform>tools</platform>
                <theme>tools</theme>
        </system>

EOF
  fi

  if [ ! "${VULKAN_SUPPORT}" = "yes" ]; then
    xmlstarlet ed --inplace -d '//choice[contains(@name, "vulkan")]' ${INSTALL}/usr/config/emulationstation/es_features.cfg
  fi

    ln -sf /usr/share/locale ${INSTALL}/usr/lib/locale

    ln -sf /usr/share/locale  ${INSTALL}/usr/config/emulationstation/locale
